domains.name: generation
domains.description: Power generation from conventional and renewable sources including CCGT, coal, nuclear, hydro, wind, solar, and biomass facilities. Manages plant operations, unit commitment, dispatch schedules, heat rate optimization, fuel inventory, emissions monitoring, and generation capacity planning. Core SCADA/DCS integration point for real-time generation telemetry via ABB Ability Symphony Plus. Supports IRP, LCOE analysis, and CAPEX planning for generation fleet.
domains.references: NERC TPL, EPA CAMD, IEC 61970 CIM

products.name: generating_unit
products.description: Master record for each individual generation unit (CCGT, coal, nuclear, hydro, wind turbine, solar array, biomass boiler) within the generation fleet. SSOT for generation unit identity across the enterprise.

products.name: unit_commitment
products.description: Transactional record of the day-ahead and intra-day unit commitment decisions for each generating unit. Captures commitment period (start/end timestamp), committed capacity (MW), minimum run time, minimum down time, startup type (hot/warm/cold), commitment source (ISO/RTO security-constrained unit commitment or self-schedule), associated DAM or RTM market interval, and commitment status. Feeds AGC and dispatch scheduling workflows. Supports NERC TOP (Transmission Operations) and IRO (Interconnection Reliability Operations) standard compliance for reliability-must-run commitments and FERC market monitoring of self-scheduled vs market-committed units.

attributes.name: transmission_path_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.path. Business justification: ISO/RTO unit commitment decisions must consider transmission path constraints and available transfer capability. Security-constrained unit commitment (SCUC) algorithms evaluate generation commitments

attributes.name: agc_participation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the unit is participating in Automatic Generation Control during this commitment period, allowing real-time dispatch adjustments for frequency regulation.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance Standard

attributes.name: ancillary_service_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this commitment includes provision of ancillary services (regulation, spinning reserve, non-spinning reserve, voltage support) in addition to energy.

attributes.name: commitment_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes providing additional context about the commitment decision, special operating instructions, or coordination requirements with transmission operators.

attributes.name: commitment_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the commitment decision. Externally-known reference number used in market submissions, dispatch communications, and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: commitment_period_end
attributes.description: End date and time of the operating period for which the unit is committed. Defines the conclusion of the commitment window.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance Standard

attributes.name: commitment_period_start
attributes.description: Start date and time of the operating period for which the unit is committed. Defines the beginning of the commitment window.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance Standard

attributes.name: commitment_reason_code
attributes.description: Code indicating the business reason for this commitment decision. Examples: economic dispatch, reliability requirement, voltage support, black start capability, renewable integration support.

attributes.name: commitment_revision_number
attributes.description: Sequential revision number for this commitment. Increments when commitment parameters are updated due to market re-runs, unit availability changes, or dispatch adjustments.

attributes.name: commitment_source
attributes.description: Origin of the commitment decision. Indicates whether commitment resulted from ISO/RTO Security-Constrained Unit Commitment (SCUC), self-schedule, reliability requirement, or other source.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: commitment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the unit commitment. Tracks progression from initial commitment decision through dispatch execution to unit synchronization and operation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|confirmed|dispatched|synchronized|operating|ramping_down|offline|cancelled|failed — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: commitment_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the commitment decision was made by the ISO/RTO or internal scheduling system. Principal business event timestamp for this transaction.

attributes.name: committed_capacity_mw
attributes.description: The committed generation capacity in megawatts (MW) for the commitment period. Represents the output level the unit is scheduled to provide.
attributes.references: IEEE 762 Standard Definitions for Use in Reporting Electric Generating Unit Reliability

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier that created this commitment record. Supports audit trail and accountability for commitment decisions.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this commitment record was first created in the system. Audit trail for record creation.

attributes.name: dispatch_priority
attributes.description: Numeric priority ranking for dispatch order. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used in economic dispatch and Automatic Generation Control (AGC) sequencing.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance Standard

attributes.name: economic_maximum_mw
attributes.description: Maximum generation level in megawatts at which the unit can operate economically under normal conditions. Represents the upper bound of the economic operating range.
attributes.references: ABB Ability Symphony Plus - Unit Performance Curves

attributes.name: economic_minimum_mw
attributes.description: Minimum stable generation level in megawatts at which the unit can operate economically. Below this level, unit efficiency degrades significantly.
attributes.references: ABB Ability Symphony Plus - Unit Performance Curves

attributes.name: estimated_co2_emissions_tons
attributes.description: Estimated carbon dioxide emissions in tons for the commitment period, calculated from fuel type, heat rate, and generation output.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 Greenhouse Gas Reporting

attributes.name: estimated_fuel_cost_usd
attributes.description: Estimated total fuel cost in US dollars for the commitment period, based on committed capacity, expected heat rate, and fuel price.

attributes.name: estimated_nox_emissions_lbs
attributes.description: Estimated nitrogen oxides emissions in pounds for the commitment period. Critical for compliance with EPA NOx Budget Trading Program and regional air quality standards.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75 Continuous Emission Monitoring

attributes.name: estimated_so2_emissions_lbs
attributes.description: Estimated sulfur dioxide emissions in pounds for the commitment period. Required for EPA Acid Rain Program compliance and SO2 allowance tracking.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75 Continuous Emission Monitoring

attributes.name: estimated_startup_cost_usd
attributes.description: Estimated cost in US dollars to start the unit for this commitment, including fuel, maintenance wear, and auxiliary power. Varies by startup type.

attributes.name: estimated_variable_om_cost_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Variable Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Cost (USD)
attributes.description: Estimated variable operations and maintenance cost in US dollars for the commitment period, based on generation output and unit-specific O&M rates.

attributes.name: expected_heat_rate_btu_per_kwh
attributes.description: Expected thermal efficiency of the unit during this commitment, measured in British Thermal Units (BTU) per kilowatt-hour. Lower values indicate higher efficiency.
attributes.references: ASME PTC 46 Performance Test Code for Overall Plant Performance

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: Primary fuel source for this commitment period. Examples: natural gas, coal, nuclear, hydro, wind, solar, biomass, oil, dual-fuel. Impacts emissions and cost calculations.

attributes.name: iso_rto_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the Independent System Operator (ISO) or Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) that issued or cleared this commitment. Examples: CAISO, PJM, ERCOT, MISO, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP.
attributes.references: NERC Functional Model - Balancing Authority Registry

attributes.name: market_interval_end
attributes.description: End timestamp of the market interval or trading period associated with this commitment. Defines the market settlement window.

attributes.name: market_interval_start
attributes.description: Start timestamp of the market interval or trading period associated with this commitment. Aligns commitment with specific market clearing results.

attributes.name: market_type
attributes.description: Type of energy market associated with this commitment. Distinguishes Day-Ahead Market (DAM), Real-Time Market (RTM), hour-ahead, intra-hour, or bilateral arrangements.

attributes.name: minimum_down_time_hours
attributes.description: Minimum offline time in hours required before the unit can be restarted. Technical constraint based on cooling requirements and equipment protection.
attributes.references: ABB Ability Symphony Plus - Unit Operating Constraints

attributes.name: minimum_run_time_hours
attributes.description: Minimum continuous operating time in hours required once the unit is started. Technical constraint based on unit design and thermal stress limits.
attributes.references: ABB Ability Symphony Plus - Unit Operating Constraints

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier that last modified this commitment record. Supports audit trail for commitment revisions.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this commitment record was last modified. Audit trail for record updates and revisions.

attributes.name: must_run_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is a reliability-must-run (RMR) commitment required for transmission system reliability, voltage support, or local capacity requirements regardless of economics.

attributes.name: ramp_rate_down_mw_per_min
attributes.description: Maximum rate at which the unit can decrease generation output, measured in megawatts per minute. Important for load-following and emergency response.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance Standard

attributes.name: ramp_rate_up_mw_per_min
attributes.description: Maximum rate at which the unit can increase generation output, measured in megawatts per minute. Critical for AGC response and frequency regulation.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance Standard

attributes.name: shutdown_time_hours
attributes.description: Expected time in hours from shutdown initiation to complete unit offline status, including controlled ramp-down and equipment securing.
attributes.references: IEEE 762 Standard Definitions for Use in Reporting Electric Generating Unit Reliability

attributes.name: startup_time_hours
attributes.description: Expected time in hours from startup initiation to unit synchronization and minimum load, based on the startup type (hot/warm/cold).
attributes.references: IEEE 762 Standard Definitions for Use in Reporting Electric Generating Unit Reliability

attributes.name: startup_type
attributes.description: Classification of the unit startup based on time offline and equipment temperature. Determines startup time, fuel consumption, and emissions profile.
attributes.references: IEEE 762 Standard Definitions for Use in Reporting Electric Generating Unit Reliability

products.name: dispatch_schedule
products.description: Hourly and sub-hourly generation dispatch instructions for each generating unit, produced by the EMS/SCADA dispatch engine or received as ISO/RTO dispatch instructions per FERC Order 764 (15-minute scheduling intervals). Captures schedule interval timestamp, scheduled output (MW), economic dispatch order, incremental cost curve reference, curtailment flag, must-run flag, AGC setpoint, and source system (ABB Symphony Plus / EMS). Links to unit commitment decisions that authorize the dispatch. Supports real-time generation control, NERC BAL standard compliance (balancing authority ACE), AGC performance scoring, and settlement reconciliation against actual output telemetry.
products.reference: NERC BAL / EMS Dispatch Instruction

attributes.name: actual_output_mw
attributes.description: The actual measured generation output in MW during this dispatch interval as reported by SCADA telemetry. Used for settlement reconciliation, AGC performance scoring, and dispatch compliance analysis. Compared against scheduled_output_mw to calculate dispatch variance.
attributes.references: NERC BAL Standards - Actual Generation Telemetry

attributes.name: agc_setpoint_mw
attributes.description: The AGC setpoint in megawatts sent to the generating unit's automatic generation control system. This is the real-time control signal that adjusts unit output to maintain system frequency and balance generation with load. May differ slightly from scheduled_output_mw due to real-time balancing requirements.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this dispatch schedule record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: curtailment_reason_code
attributes.description: Categorical code indicating the reason for curtailment if the is_curtailed flag is true. Supports root cause analysis of generation curtailment events and regulatory reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: transmission_constraint|over_generation|market_condition|environmental_limit|fuel_limitation|equipment_derate|none — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: dispatch_acknowledgement_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the generating unit operator or control system acknowledged receipt of this dispatch instruction. Used to measure response time and operator compliance.

attributes.name: dispatch_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the generating unit's actual output was within acceptable tolerance of the scheduled output for this dispatch interval. True if compliant, false if variance exceeded threshold. Used for operator performance evaluation and NERC compliance reporting.

attributes.name: dispatch_instruction_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this dispatch instruction was issued by the EMS/SCADA system or received from the ISO/RTO. Represents when the instruction was communicated to plant operators or control systems. Used for performance analysis and compliance verification.

attributes.name: dispatch_priority_code
attributes.description: Categorical code indicating the dispatch priority classification of this generating unit for this interval. Baseload units run continuously, intermediate units cycle daily, peaking units run during high-demand periods, renewable units dispatch when available, emergency units are last resort, and test dispatches are for commissioning or maintenance verification.
attributes.references: NERC Glossary of Terms - Generation Classification

attributes.name: dispatch_schedule_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the dispatch schedule. Human-readable reference number used in operational communications and SCADA displays.
attributes.references: ABB Ability Symphony Plus - Dispatch Management

attributes.name: dispatch_source_system
attributes.description: The source system that generated this dispatch instruction. Identifies whether the dispatch came from the internal EMS/SCADA dispatch engine (ABB Symphony Plus), an external ISO/RTO market dispatch, or manual operator entry.
attributes.references: ABB Ability Symphony Plus - System Integration

attributes.name: dispatch_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the dispatch schedule. Tracks whether the dispatch instruction is pending execution, actively being followed, completed, or cancelled.
attributes.references: ABB Ability Symphony Plus - Dispatch Lifecycle

attributes.name: dispatch_variance_mw
attributes.description: The difference between actual output and scheduled output in MW (actual_output_mw minus scheduled_output_mw). Positive values indicate over-generation; negative values indicate under-generation. Used for AGC performance scoring and NERC BAL compliance reporting.
attributes.references: NERC BAL Standards - Area Control Error (ACE)

attributes.name: economic_dispatch_order
attributes.description: The merit order ranking of this generating unit in the economic dispatch stack for this interval. Lower numbers indicate lower incremental cost and higher dispatch priority. Used for economic optimization of generation fleet.

attributes.name: emissions_rate_co2_lbs_per_mwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Emissions Rate Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Pounds (lbs) per Megawatt-Hour (MWh)
attributes.description: The carbon dioxide emissions rate in pounds per MWh for this generating unit at the scheduled output level during this dispatch interval. Used for environmental compliance reporting, carbon accounting, and emissions trading programs.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act - CO2 Emissions Reporting

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: The primary fuel type used by the generating unit for this dispatch interval. Supports fuel-specific dispatch optimization, emissions tracking, and renewable portfolio standard (RPS) compliance reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: natural_gas|coal|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar|biomass|oil|geothermal — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: heat_rate_btu_per_kwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Heat Rate British Thermal Units (BTU) per Kilowatt-Hour (kWh)
attributes.description: The heat rate in BTU per kWh for this generating unit at the scheduled output level during this dispatch interval. Represents the thermal efficiency of the unit. Lower heat rates indicate higher efficiency. Used for fuel cost calculation and LCOE analysis.
attributes.references: DOE Energy Efficiency Standards - Heat Rate

attributes.name: incremental_cost_curve_reference
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the incremental cost curve (heat rate curve) used to calculate the economic dispatch order for this unit during this interval. Links to the cost function that defines the relationship between output level and marginal cost.

attributes.name: is_curtailed
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this dispatch schedule represents a curtailment instruction (reduction from maximum available output). True if the unit is being dispatched below its available capacity due to transmission constraints, over-generation conditions, or market conditions.

attributes.name: is_must_run
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this generating unit is operating under a must-run designation for this interval. Must-run units are required to operate for reliability, voltage support, or contractual reasons regardless of economic dispatch order.

attributes.name: iso_rto_dispatch_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Independent System Operator (ISO) / Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) Dispatch ID
attributes.description: External dispatch instruction identifier from the ISO or RTO if this dispatch schedule originated from a wholesale market dispatch signal. Used for settlement reconciliation and market compliance verification.

attributes.name: market_type
attributes.description: The type of energy market or scheduling process that produced this dispatch instruction. Distinguishes between day-ahead market (DAM), real-time market (RTM), ancillary service dispatch, capacity market obligations, bilateral contracts, or internal economic dispatch.

attributes.name: maximum_generation_limit_mw
attributes.description: The maximum available generation capacity in MW for this generating unit during this dispatch interval. Represents the technical upper bound considering current equipment status, ambient conditions, and operational constraints. Used to validate dispatch feasibility.
attributes.references: NERC MOD Standards - Unit Operating Limits

attributes.name: minimum_generation_limit_mw
attributes.description: The minimum stable generation level in MW for this generating unit during this dispatch interval. Represents the technical lower bound below which the unit cannot operate reliably. Used to validate dispatch feasibility.
attributes.references: NERC MOD Standards - Unit Operating Limits

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this dispatch schedule record was last modified. Audit trail field for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: must_run_reason_code
attributes.description: Categorical code indicating the reason for must-run designation if the is_must_run flag is true. Documents the reliability or contractual basis for out-of-merit dispatch.

attributes.name: operator_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for plant operators or dispatch coordinators to record notes, observations, or special instructions related to this dispatch schedule. Supports operational knowledge capture and incident investigation.

attributes.name: ramp_rate_mw_per_minute
attributes.description: The maximum allowable rate of change in generation output in MW per minute for this dispatch interval. Constrains how quickly the unit can increase or decrease output to protect equipment and maintain grid stability.
attributes.references: NERC BAL Standards - Ramp Rate Limits

attributes.name: regulation_down_mw
attributes.description: The amount of downward regulation capacity in MW that this generating unit is providing during this dispatch interval. Regulation down is the ability to decrease output below the scheduled setpoint to provide frequency regulation ancillary service.

attributes.name: regulation_up_mw
attributes.description: The amount of upward regulation capacity in MW that this generating unit is providing during this dispatch interval. Regulation up is the ability to increase output above the scheduled setpoint to provide frequency regulation ancillary service.

attributes.name: schedule_interval_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp marking the end of the dispatch interval. Defines the duration for which this dispatch instruction is valid.

attributes.name: schedule_interval_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp marking the beginning of the dispatch interval. Represents the real-world time when this dispatch instruction becomes effective. Aligns with FERC Order 764 15-minute scheduling intervals or ISO/RTO market intervals.

attributes.name: scheduled_output_mw
attributes.description: The target generation output in megawatts (MW) that the generating unit is instructed to produce during this dispatch interval. Core dispatch setpoint used by plant operators and AGC systems.

attributes.name: spinning_reserve_mw
attributes.description: The amount of spinning reserve capacity in MW that this generating unit is providing during this dispatch interval. Spinning reserve is synchronized generation capacity that can respond within 10 minutes to replace lost generation.

Captures interval timestamp (5-min, 15-min, hourly), gross generation (MWh), net generation (MWh), auxiliary load (MWh), reactive power (MVAr), power factor, frequency deviation, and data quality flag. Primary source for settlement metering, NERC compliance, and LCOE calculations.

attributes.name: dispatch_status

attributes.references: FERC Order 888 Open Access Transmission Tariff, NAESB WEQ-001 Wholesale Electric Quadrant Standards

attributes.name: emissions_co2_tons
attributes.description: Estimated carbon dioxide emissions produced during the interval, measured in metric tons. Calculated from fuel consumption and emission factors. Used for environmental compliance reporting and carbon accounting.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75 Continuous Emission Monitoring, EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP)

attributes.name: emissions_nox_lbs
attributes.description: Estimated nitrogen oxides emissions produced during the interval, measured in pounds. Critical for air quality compliance and emissions trading programs.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75 Continuous Emission Monitoring, Clean Air Act Title IV Acid Rain Program

attributes.name: emissions_so2_lbs
attributes.description: Estimated sulfur dioxide emissions produced during the interval, measured in pounds. Used for environmental compliance and emissions allowance tracking.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75 Continuous Emission Monitoring, Clean Air Act Title IV Acid Rain Program

attributes.name: forced_outage_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether the generating unit experienced a forced outage or unplanned derate during this interval. Used for reliability reporting and NERC GADS compliance.
attributes.references: NERC GADS (Generating Availability Data System), IEEE 762 Standard Definitions for Use in Reporting Electric Generating Unit Reliability

attributes.name: frequency_deviation_hz
attributes.description: Deviation from nominal grid frequency (typically 60 Hz in North America or 50 Hz elsewhere) during the interval, measured in hertz. Used for grid stability monitoring and NERC compliance reporting.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance, NERC BAL-003 Frequency Response and Frequency Bias Setting

attributes.name: fuel_consumption_mmbtu
attributes.description: Total fuel consumed by the generating unit during the interval, measured in million British Thermal Units (MMBtu). Used for fuel inventory management, cost allocation, and emissions calculations.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75 Continuous Emission Monitoring, FERC Form 1 Electric Plant Statistics

attributes.name: gross_generation_mwh
attributes.description: Total electrical energy generated by the unit during the interval, measured in megawatt-hours (MWh), before deducting auxiliary load or station service. Primary metric for generation capacity and output tracking.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-005 Automatic Generation Control, IEEE 762 Standard Definitions for Use in Reporting Electric Generating Unit Reliability

attributes.name: heat_rate_btu_per_kwh
attributes.description: Thermal efficiency of the generating unit during the interval, expressed as British Thermal Units (BTU) of fuel input per kilowatt-hour of electrical output. Lower values indicate higher efficiency. Critical for LCOE analysis and fuel cost optimization.
attributes.references: ASME PTC 6 Steam Turbines, EPA 40 CFR Part 60 Standards of Performance for New Stationary Sources

attributes.name: historian_tag_name
attributes.description: The specific tag name or point identifier in the OSIsoft PI historian or equivalent time-series database that stores this telemetry reading. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and integration with real-time monitoring systems.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI System Architecture, NERC CIP-008 Incident Reporting and Response Planning

attributes.name: interval_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The duration of the measurement interval in minutes. Common values include 5, 15, or 60 minutes. Used to normalize interval data for aggregation and settlement calculations.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ-001 Wholesale Electric Quadrant Standards

attributes.name: interval_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise timestamp marking the end of the measurement interval for this telemetry reading. Represents the real-world event time when the generation output was recorded by the DCS or SCADA system. Typically aligned to 5-minute, 15-minute, or hourly intervals depending on settlement and reporting requirements.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-004 Event Reporting, FERC Order 2222 Telemetry Requirements

attributes.name: market_settlement_amount_usd
attributes.description: Financial settlement amount for this generation interval in US dollars, calculated based on net generation and applicable LMP or contract rates. Used for revenue recognition and financial reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2000 Regional Transmission Organizations, SOX Section 404 Internal Controls

attributes.name: net_generation_mwh
attributes.description: Net electrical energy delivered to the grid during the interval, measured in megawatt-hours (MWh), after deducting auxiliary load and station service consumption. Used for settlement metering, revenue calculations, and LCOE analysis.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1 Electric Plant Statistics, NERC MOD-032 Data for Power System Modeling

attributes.name: planned_outage_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether the generating unit was on a scheduled planned outage or maintenance during this interval. Used for capacity planning and reliability reporting.
attributes.references: NERC GADS (Generating Availability Data System), IEEE 762 Standard Definitions for Use in Reporting Electric Generating Unit Reliability

attributes.name: power_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of real power to apparent power during the interval, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1. Indicates the efficiency of power delivery and compliance with grid interconnection standards. Typical range: 0.85 to 1.00.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547 Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources, NERC PRC-024 Generator Frequency and Voltage Protective Relay Settings

attributes.name: ramp_rate_mw_per_min
attributes.description: Rate of change in generation output during the interval, measured in megawatts per minute. Indicates the unit's ability to respond to dispatch signals and grid frequency changes. Critical for AGC and frequency response compliance.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 Real Power Balancing Control Performance, FERC Order 755 Frequency Regulation Compensation

attributes.name: reactive_power_mvar
attributes.description: Reactive power output during the interval, measured in megavolt-amperes reactive (MVAr). Critical for voltage support, grid stability, and compliance with interconnection agreements.
attributes.references: NERC VAR-002 Generator Operation for Maintaining Network Voltage Schedules, FERC Order 827 Reactive Power Requirements

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this telemetry record was first inserted into the lakehouse silver layer. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and ETL troubleshooting. Distinct from interval_timestamp which represents the business event time.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standards, SOX Section 404 Internal Controls

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this telemetry record was last modified in the lakehouse silver layer. Used for change tracking, audit trails, and data quality monitoring. Updated whenever VEE processes or manual corrections are applied.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standards, SOX Section 404 Internal Controls

attributes.name: scada_source_system
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Source System
attributes.description: Identifier of the SCADA or DCS system that originated this telemetry reading. Typically references ABB Ability Symphony Plus, OSIsoft PI, or other plant control systems. Used for data lineage and troubleshooting.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-007 Systems Security Management, IEC 61850 Communication Networks and Systems for Power Utility Automation

attributes.name: settlement_meter_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether this telemetry reading is used for financial settlement with the ISO/RTO or wholesale market. True indicates the reading is settlement-quality and used for revenue calculations.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2000 Regional Transmission Organizations, NAESB WEQ-012 Measurement and Verification of Wholesale Electricity

attributes.name: validation_method
attributes.description: Method used to validate or estimate the telemetry reading. Indicates whether the data was automatically validated, manually reviewed, processed through Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) algorithms, or verified by SCADA/historian systems.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM VEE Standards, NERC MOD-032 Data for Power System Modeling

attributes.name: voltage_kv
attributes.description: Terminal voltage at the generator output during the interval, measured in kilovolts (kV). Used for voltage regulation monitoring and compliance with interconnection requirements.
attributes.references: NERC VAR-001 Voltage and Reactive Control, IEEE C37.106 Guide for Abnormal Frequency Protection for Power Generating Plants

products.name: heat_rate_test
products.description: Records of periodic performance and capability tests conducted on generating units. For heat rate tests: captures test date, test type (acceptance, periodic, diagnostic), measured net heat rate (BTU/kWh), design heat rate, ambient temperature, load level tested (MW), fuel type and HHV used, test duration, and deviation from design. For capacity tests: captures demonstrated net capability (MW), net dependable capability (MW), test type (summer peak, winter peak, seasonal), ambient conditions, test duration, and ISO/RTO submission status. Used for LCOE analysis, IRP modeling, NERC MOD-025 compliance, and capacity market accreditation. SSOT for all generating unit performance and capability test results.
products.reference: NERC MOD-027 / ASME PTC 46 Performance Test

attributes.name: heat_rate_test_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the heat rate test record. Primary key for the heat_rate_test product.

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.control_area. Business justification: Heat rate tests are submitted to ISO/RTO markets by control area for NERC compliance (FAC-001/002) and market offer validation. The test already has iso_rto_submission_flag and nerc_compliance_flag; a

attributes.name: heat_generating_unit_id
attributes.description: FK to generation.generating_unit.generating_unit_id — Performance tests (heat rate and capacity) are conducted on specific generating units. generating_unit_id is required for NERC MOD compliance tracking and IRP modeling.

attributes.name: inspection_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.inspection. Business justification: Heat rate tests are formal performance inspections required by NERC and ISO/RTO market rules. Linking heat_rate_test to asset.inspection integrates performance test results with the asset inspection r

attributes.name: market_bid_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to trading.market_bid. Business justification: ISO/RTO rules (FERC Order 831) require heat rate test results to support bid cost recovery in market bids. This FK creates the audit trail from validated heat rate test to the cost-based offer curve s

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: Heat rate tests satisfy ISO/RTO market qualification rules and FERC requirements for market-based rate authority. Essential for market participation compliance, rate case support, and regulatory submi

attributes.name: primary_generating_unit_id
attributes.description: FK to generation.generating_unit.generating_unit_id — Every performance/capability test is conducted on a specific generating unit. Without this FK, test results cannot be linked to the unit they measure, breaking NERC MOD-025 compliance and capacity acc

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Business justification: Heat rate test results are submitted to ISO/RTO and FERC as regulatory performance filings (e.g., NERC MOD-027 heat rate verification submissions). The existing iso_rto_submission_flag and iso_rto_sub

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.work_order. Business justification: Heat rate tests are performed as part of commissioning work orders, post-maintenance validation, or ISO/RTO performance verification requirements. Linking tests to work orders tracks labor costs, sche

attributes.name: acceptance_criteria_description
attributes.description: Textual description of the acceptance criteria applied to this test, including tolerance bands, correction factors, and contractual requirements. Provides context for the test acceptance flag.

attributes.name: ambient_pressure_psia
attributes.description: Ambient barometric pressure in pounds per square inch absolute during the test. Affects air density and combustion turbine performance.
attributes.references: ASME PTC 46 - Performance Test Code for Gas Turbines

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_f
attributes.description: Ambient air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit during the test. Ambient conditions significantly affect gas turbine and combined cycle performance, so temperature correction factors are applied to normalize results.
attributes.references: ASME PTC 46 - Performance Test Code for Gas Turbines

attributes.name: auxiliary_load_mw
attributes.description: Station auxiliary electrical load in megawatts during the test period. Includes cooling water pumps, fans, fuel handling equipment, and other plant auxiliary systems.

attributes.name: corrected_net_heat_rate_btu_per_kwh
attributes.description: Net heat rate corrected to ISO base conditions (59°F, 14.7 psia, 60% RH) or other contractual reference conditions. Allows apples-to-apples comparison across tests conducted under different ambient conditions.
attributes.references: ASME PTC 46 - Performance Test Code for Gas Turbines

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this heat rate test record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage.

attributes.name: design_net_heat_rate_btu_per_kwh
attributes.description: The design or guaranteed net heat rate for the generating unit at the tested load level and ambient conditions, expressed in BTU/kWh. Used as the baseline for performance comparison.

attributes.name: fuel_consumption_rate
attributes.description: Rate of fuel consumption during the test period. Units vary by fuel type (e.g., scf/hr for natural gas, lb/hr for coal, gallons/hr for oil). Used to calculate total heat input.

attributes.name: fuel_consumption_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the fuel consumption rate. Must align with the fuel type and HHV units for accurate heat rate calculation.

attributes.name: fuel_hhv_btu_per_unit
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fuel Higher Heating Value (HHV) (BTU per Unit)
attributes.description: Higher heating value of the fuel used during the test, expressed in BTU per unit (e.g., BTU/scf for natural gas, BTU/lb for coal). HHV is used in heat rate calculations to determine thermal efficiency.
attributes.references: ASTM D3588 - Standard Practice for Calculating Heat Value

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: Type of fuel consumed during the heat rate test. Heat rate calculations require accurate fuel heating value and composition data specific to the fuel type.

attributes.name: gross_output_mw
attributes.description: Gross electrical output of the generating unit during the test in megawatts, measured at the generator terminals before auxiliary load deduction.

attributes.name: heat_rate_deviation_percent
attributes.description: Percentage deviation of measured heat rate from design heat rate. Positive values indicate performance degradation (higher heat rate than design). Negative values indicate better-than-design performance. Calculated as ((measured - design) / design) * 100.

attributes.name: iso_rto_submission_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: ISO/RTO (Independent System Operator/Regional Transmission Organization) Submission Date
attributes.description: Date on which the test results were submitted to the ISO or RTO. Null if not submitted.

attributes.name: iso_rto_submission_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: ISO/RTO (Independent System Operator/Regional Transmission Organization) Submission Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this test result was submitted to the ISO or RTO for capacity market accreditation or resource adequacy purposes. True if submitted, False if not.

attributes.name: load_level_percent
attributes.description: The load level at which the test was conducted, expressed as a percentage of the unit's rated net capacity. Heat rate varies with load level, so this context is critical for performance analysis.

attributes.name: measured_net_heat_rate_btu_per_kwh
attributes.description: The actual net heat rate measured during the test, expressed in British Thermal Units per kilowatt-hour. Lower values indicate better thermal efficiency. This is the primary performance metric for generating unit efficiency and is used for LCOE analysis and IRP modeling.
attributes.references: ASME PTC 46 - Performance Test Code for Gas Turbines

attributes.name: nerc_compliance_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: NERC (North American Electric Reliability Corporation) Compliance Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this test was conducted to satisfy NERC MOD-025 generator verification requirements. True if conducted for NERC compliance, False otherwise.

attributes.name: net_output_mw
attributes.description: Net electrical output of the generating unit during the test in megawatts, measured at the point of interconnection after deducting station auxiliary load. This is the load level at which the heat rate was tested.

attributes.name: relative_humidity_percent
attributes.description: Relative humidity as a percentage during the test. Humidity affects combustion turbine performance and is used in correction factor calculations.
attributes.references: ASME PTC 46 - Performance Test Code for Gas Turbines

attributes.name: scada_data_source
attributes.business_glossary_term: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) Data Source
attributes.description: Identifier of the SCADA or DCS system from which real-time telemetry data was collected during the test. Typically references OSIsoft PI tags or ABB Ability Symphony Plus data points.

attributes.name: test_acceptance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the test results met acceptance criteria. True if the measured heat rate was within contractual tolerance of design heat rate, False if performance was out of tolerance.

attributes.name: test_date
attributes.description: The date on which the heat rate test was conducted. Primary business event timestamp for the test.

attributes.name: test_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the heat rate test in minutes. ASME PTC 46 typically requires minimum 2-4 hours of steady-state operation for valid heat rate tests.
attributes.references: ASME PTC 46 - Performance Test Code for Gas Turbines

attributes.name: test_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the heat rate test data collection concluded. Used to calculate test duration and validate steady-state conditions.

attributes.name: test_engineer_name
attributes.description: Name of the lead engineer responsible for conducting and supervising the heat rate test. Provides accountability and contact for test methodology questions.

attributes.name: test_notes
attributes.description: Free-form notes documenting test conditions, anomalies, equipment issues, or other contextual information relevant to interpreting the test results.

attributes.name: test_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the heat rate test. Externally-known unique code used for tracking and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: test_report_document_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the formal test report document stored in the document management system. Links to detailed test methodology, data sheets, and analysis.

attributes.name: test_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the heat rate test data collection began. Used for correlating with SCADA telemetry and operational logs.

attributes.name: test_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the heat rate test. Scheduled tests are planned but not started. In-progress tests are actively being conducted. Completed tests have finished data collection. Validated tests have passed quality review. Rejected tests failed validation criteria. Cancelled tests were aborted before completion.

attributes.name: test_type
attributes.description: Classification of the heat rate test. Acceptance tests validate new or refurbished units against design specifications. Periodic tests are routine performance assessments. Diagnostic tests investigate performance degradation. Baseline tests establish reference performance. Warranty tests verify vendor guarantees. Performance verification tests support capacity market accreditation.
attributes.references: ASME PTC 46 - Performance Test Code for Gas Turbines

attributes.name: test_witness_organization
attributes.description: Name of the independent third-party organization that witnessed the test, if applicable. Common for acceptance tests, warranty tests, and ISO/RTO capacity accreditation tests.

attributes.name: total_heat_input_mmbtu
attributes.description: Total heat input to the generating unit during the test period in million BTU. Calculated as fuel consumption rate multiplied by fuel HHV and test duration. Used as the numerator in heat rate calculation.
attributes.references: ASME PTC 46 - Performance Test Code for Gas Turbines

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this heat rate test record was last modified. Audit trail for data lineage and change tracking.

attributes.name: validated_by
attributes.description: Name of the engineer or manager who validated and approved the test results. Provides accountability for data quality.

attributes.name: validation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the test results were validated and approved. Null if validation is pending or rejected.

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Status of the engineering validation review for the test results. Pending indicates awaiting review. Approved indicates results passed quality checks. Rejected indicates results failed validation. Under review indicates active engineering analysis.

products.name: fuel_inventory
products.description: Current and historical fuel inventory positions and receipt transactions for thermal generation facilities. For inventory positions: tracks fuel type (natural gas, coal, nuclear fuel, oil, biomass), inventory quantity (tons, MMBtu, or fuel assemblies), storage location, minimum operating reserve level, days-of-supply, and unit cost ($/MMBtu). For receipt transactions: captures receipt date, quantity received, supplier name, contract reference, invoice number, as-received heat content (BTU/lb or BTU/SCF), sulfur content, moisture content, transportation mode, and unit cost. Supports fuel supply planning, O&M cost tracking, generation availability forecasting, EIA Form 923 reporting, and emissions calculations. SSOT for fuel stock position, receipt transactions, and fuel quality data at generation facilities.
products.reference: EIA Form 923 Fuel Receipts / SAP MM Material Stock

attributes.name: fuel_inventory_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the fuel inventory record. Primary key for fuel inventory positions and receipt transactions at thermal generation facilities.

attributes.name: fuel_contract_id
attributes.description: FK to generation.fuel_contract.fuel_contract_id — Fuel receipts (now merged into fuel_inventory) reference the supply contract under which fuel was delivered. fuel_contract_id is needed for contract compliance monitoring and cost allocation.

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific generation unit consuming or storing this fuel. Links to the generation unit master data.

attributes.name: primary_power_plant_id
attributes.description: FK to generation.power_plant.power_plant_id — Fuel inventory is tracked at the plant/facility level (coal piles, gas interconnects, oil tanks are plant-level assets). power_plant_id is required on fuel_inventory for fuel supply planning and gener

attributes.name: registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.registry. Business justification: Fuel storage tanks, coal yards, and gas storage facilities are physical assets in the registry. Linking fuel inventory to the storage asset registry record supports asset condition monitoring, regulat

attributes.name: adjustment_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for inventory adjustments or corrections. Examples include physical inventory count variance, measurement error correction, fuel quality degradation, evaporation loss, or system reconciliation. Required for SOX audit trail and internal controls.

attributes.name: carbon_content_percent
attributes.description: Carbon content of the fuel as a percentage by weight. Used to calculate carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions for EPA greenhouse gas reporting, carbon pricing programs, and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance. Higher carbon content increases CO2 emissions per unit of energy.

attributes.name: chlorine_content_ppm
attributes.description: Chlorine content of the fuel measured in parts per million (ppm). Contributes to boiler corrosion and hydrochloric acid (HCl) emissions. Monitored for EPA air toxics compliance and boiler materials integrity management.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text comments or notes regarding this fuel inventory record. Captures operational context, special handling instructions, quality issues, delivery exceptions, or other relevant information for fuel management and audit purposes.

attributes.name: contract_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier of the fuel supply contract or Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) governing this receipt. Links fuel deliveries to contractual terms, pricing agreements, and procurement commitments. Business-confidential contract data.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fuel inventory record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and SOX compliance for financial controls. Distinct from inventory date or receipt timestamp which represent business event times.

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of data quality status for this fuel inventory record. Verified indicates quality-assured data, estimated for calculated or interpolated values, pending verification for preliminary data awaiting confirmation, failed validation for records with quality issues requiring correction.

attributes.name: days_of_supply
attributes.description: Calculated number of days the current fuel inventory can support generation operations at average burn rate. Critical metric for fuel supply planning, generation availability forecasting, and risk management during supply disruptions.

attributes.name: eia_plant_code
attributes.description: Federal Energy Information Administration (EIA) unique plant identifier. Required for EIA Form 923 monthly fuel receipt and cost reporting. Links internal fuel inventory data to federal regulatory reporting requirements.

attributes.name: ferc_account_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
attributes.description: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Uniform System of Accounts code for fuel inventory accounting. Typically account 151 for fuel stock. Required for FERC Form 1 financial reporting and rate case filings.

attributes.name: fixed_carbon_percent
attributes.description: Fixed carbon content of coal as a percentage by weight. Represents the solid combustible residue after volatile matter is driven off. Higher fixed carbon indicates higher energy content and coal rank. Critical for coal quality classification and heat rate calculations.

attributes.name: inventory_date
attributes.description: Date of the inventory position snapshot or receipt transaction. For positions, represents the as-of date for stock levels. For receipts, represents the date fuel was received at the facility.

attributes.name: inventory_status
attributes.description: Current status of the fuel inventory. Available for generation use, reserved for specific unit commitment, in transit from supplier, quarantined pending quality verification, or consumed (historical record). Supports inventory allocation and generation scheduling.

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: Supplier invoice number for the fuel receipt transaction. Links fuel deliveries to accounts payable, supports invoice reconciliation, and provides audit trail for financial controls per Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) requirements.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fuel inventory record was last modified. Tracks data changes for audit purposes, supports change data capture for downstream analytics, and provides data freshness indicator for operational dashboards.

attributes.name: mercury_content_ppm
attributes.description: Mercury content of coal fuel measured in parts per million (ppm). Required for EPA Mercury and Air Toxics Standards (MATS) compliance. High mercury content requires additional emissions controls such as activated carbon injection or scrubber upgrades.
attributes.references: EPA Mercury and Air Toxics Standards

attributes.name: minimum_operating_reserve
attributes.description: Minimum fuel quantity required to maintain safe and reliable plant operations. Expressed in same unit of measure as quantity. Used for fuel supply planning and procurement trigger points to ensure generation availability.

attributes.name: nitrogen_content_percent
attributes.description: Nitrogen content of the fuel as a percentage by weight. Affects nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions formation during combustion. Critical for EPA air quality compliance, NOx emissions calculations, and selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system design.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act NOx Standards

attributes.name: origin_location
attributes.description: Geographic origin or source location of the fuel. Examples include coal mine name and state, natural gas production basin, nuclear fuel fabrication facility, or biomass harvest region. Supports supply chain tracking and sourcing analysis.

attributes.name: quality_certification_number
attributes.description: Certificate or lab analysis number documenting fuel quality test results. Links to third-party laboratory reports for heat content, sulfur, moisture, and ash analysis. Provides audit trail for fuel quality assurance and contract compliance.

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: Quantity of fuel in inventory or received. Measured in tons for coal and biomass, Million British Thermal Units (MMBtu) for natural gas and oil, or fuel assemblies for nuclear fuel. Precision supports accurate fuel accounting and EIA reporting.

attributes.name: receipt_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when fuel was received at the generation facility. Captured from weigh station, pipeline meter, or receiving dock systems. Supports just-in-time inventory management and delivery performance tracking.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the operational system that originated this fuel inventory record. Examples include SAP Materials Management (MM), OSIsoft PI historian, plant fuel management system, or manual entry. Supports data lineage and system-of-record tracking.

attributes.name: total_cost
attributes.description: Total cost of the fuel inventory position or receipt transaction in US dollars. Calculated as quantity multiplied by unit cost, adjusted for energy content. Used for financial reporting, Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) and Operational Expenditure (OPEX) tracking, and regulatory rate case filings.

attributes.name: transaction_type
attributes.description: Type of fuel inventory transaction. Position represents current stock level, receipt captures incoming fuel deliveries, consumption tracks fuel burned for generation, adjustment handles inventory corrections, and transfer records inter-facility movements.

attributes.name: transportation_mode
attributes.description: Method of fuel transportation for receipt transactions. Rail for coal unit trains, truck for short-haul deliveries, pipeline for natural gas, barge for waterway transport, or ship for international coal imports. Affects delivery costs and supply chain logistics.

attributes.name: unit_cost
attributes.description: Cost per unit of fuel expressed in dollars per Million British Thermal Units ($/MMBtu). Supports Operations and Maintenance (O&M) cost tracking, Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) analysis, and generation dispatch economics. Business-confidential pricing data.

attributes.name: volatile_matter_percent
attributes.description: Volatile matter content of coal as a percentage by weight. Indicates the portion of coal that vaporizes when heated. Affects ignition characteristics, flame stability, and combustion efficiency. Higher volatile matter improves combustion but may increase emissions.

products.name: emissions_reading
products.description: Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS) data and emissions allowance registry records for generating units subject to environmental compliance programs. For CEMS data: captures measurement timestamp, pollutant type (SO2, NOx, CO2, Hg, PM), measured emission rate (lbs/MMBtu or lbs/hr), gross load, operating hour flag, CEMS monitor status, substitute data flag, and QA/QC certification status. For allowances: captures allowance type, vintage year, quantity (tons), program (EPA ARP, RGGI, California Cap-and-Trade), acquisition date/cost, account balance, and transfer history. Required for EPA Part 75 compliance, cap-and-trade program compliance, and carbon cost accounting. SSOT for generation emissions monitoring and allowance management.
products.reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 75 CEMS / Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: emissions_reading_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the emissions reading record. Primary key for the emissions_reading product.

attributes.name: cems_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.registry. Business justification: CEMS devices are physical assets in the registry. EPA 40 CFR Part 75 compliance requires linking emissions readings to the specific certified CEMS monitor for QA certification tracking, calibration au

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.control_area. Business justification: Emissions reporting often aggregates by control area for regional air quality compliance (e.g., RGGI, CAIR). Required for EPA and state environmental reporting.

attributes.name: environmental_permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.environmental_permit. Business justification: CEMS emissions readings must be validated against the specific Title V or state environmental permit emission limits for that unit. Compliance officers compare real-time readings against permit thresh

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: Each emissions measurement ties to specific regulatory obligations (Clean Air Act, state SIPs, emissions trading programs) for compliance demonstration, allowance tracking, and violation detection. Cr

attributes.name: outage_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to outage.event. Business justification: EPA CEMS regulations require substitute data methodology when a CEMS monitor is offline during a unit outage. emissions_reading has substitute_data_flag and substitute_data_method; linking to the outa

attributes.name: power_plant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the generation facility where this emissions reading was recorded. A facility may contain multiple generating units.

attributes.name: primary_generating_unit_id
attributes.description: FK to generation.generating_unit.generating_unit_id — CEMS data is monitored per generating unit (each unit has its own CEMS stack). generating_unit_id is required for EPA Part 75 compliance reporting which is unit-level.

attributes.name: allowance_deduction_required
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether emissions allowances must be surrendered for this reading under cap-and-trade compliance programs. True if allowance deduction is required, False if not required or if the unit is exempt.

attributes.name: allowance_quantity_deducted
attributes.description: The quantity of emissions allowances (in tons) deducted from the facility's allowance account to cover the emissions recorded in this reading. Only populated for cap-and-trade compliance programs.

attributes.name: allowance_vintage_year
attributes.description: The vintage year of the emissions allowances used to cover this reading. Allowances are typically issued for specific compliance years and may be banked or borrowed across years subject to program rules.

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_f
attributes.description: The ambient air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit at the time of the emissions measurement. Used for temperature correction factors in emissions calculations.

attributes.name: barometric_pressure_inhg
attributes.description: The barometric pressure in inches of mercury (inHg) at the time of the emissions measurement. Used for pressure correction factors in emissions calculations.

attributes.name: carbon_cost_usd
attributes.description: The calculated carbon cost in US dollars associated with this emissions reading, based on allowance market prices or internal carbon pricing. Used for carbon cost accounting and financial planning.

attributes.name: compliance_program
attributes.description: The environmental compliance program under which this emissions reading is reported. EPA_ARP (Acid Rain Program), RGGI (Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative), California_Cap_and_Trade, CSAPR (Cross-State Air Pollution Rule), MATS (Mercury and Air Toxics Standards), State_SIP (State Implementation Plan).

attributes.name: data_quality_indicator
attributes.description: Overall data quality indicator for this emissions reading based on QA/QC test results and validation rules. Passed indicates the reading meets all quality standards, failed indicates quality issues, not_available indicates quality assessment is incomplete, conditionally_valid indicates the reading is usable subject to documented conditions.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The name of the source system that provided this emissions reading data. Typically ABB Ability Symphony Plus DCS, OSIsoft PI Historian, or direct CEMS data acquisition system.

attributes.name: emission_rate
attributes.description: The measured emission rate for the pollutant. Units depend on pollutant type and are specified in emission_rate_unit field.

attributes.name: emission_rate_unit
attributes.description: The unit of measure for the emission rate. Common units include lbs/MMBtu (pounds per million British thermal units), lbs/hr (pounds per hour), tons/hr, kg/MWh (kilograms per megawatt-hour), g/kWh (grams per kilowatt-hour).

attributes.name: epa_submission_date
attributes.description: The date when this emissions reading was submitted to the EPA through ECMPS. Only populated when submitted_to_epa_flag is True.

attributes.name: flow_rate_scfh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Flow Rate (SCFH - Standard Cubic Feet per Hour)
attributes.description: The volumetric flow rate of exhaust gas in standard cubic feet per hour (SCFH) at the time of the emissions measurement. Used for total mass emissions calculations.

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: The primary fuel type being consumed by the generating unit during this emissions measurement. Used for emissions factor calculations and compliance program categorization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: coal|natural_gas|oil|biomass|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: gross_load_mw
attributes.description: The gross electrical load output of the generating unit in megawatts (MW) at the time of the emissions measurement. Used for emissions rate calculations and compliance verification.

attributes.name: heat_input_mmbtu
attributes.description: The total heat input to the generating unit in millions of British thermal units (MMBtu) during the measurement period. Used for emissions rate calculations and fuel consumption analysis.

attributes.name: measurement_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the emissions measurement was recorded by the CEMS (Continuous Emissions Monitoring System). This is the principal business event timestamp for the reading.

attributes.name: moisture_content_percent
attributes.description: The moisture content percentage in the exhaust gas stream at the time of the emissions measurement. Used for dry-basis emissions rate calculations.

attributes.name: monitor_status
attributes.description: The operational status of the CEMS monitor at the time of the reading. Operational indicates normal functioning, calibration indicates the monitor was being calibrated, maintenance indicates scheduled maintenance, failed indicates equipment failure, out_of_service indicates the monitor was not in service.

attributes.name: operating_hour_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the generating unit was in operation during this measurement hour. True if operating, False if not operating. Used for compliance hour calculations.

attributes.name: operating_mode
attributes.description: The operating mode of the generating unit at the time of the emissions measurement. Baseload indicates continuous operation, cycling indicates variable operation, peaking indicates high-demand operation, startup/shutdown indicate transitional states, standby indicates ready but not generating.

attributes.name: orispl_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: ORISPL (Office of Regulatory Information Systems Plant Location) Code
attributes.description: The unique EPA-assigned ORISPL code identifying the power plant facility. This is the standard identifier used in all EPA emissions reporting systems.

attributes.name: oxygen_concentration_percent
attributes.description: The oxygen concentration percentage in the exhaust gas stream at the time of the emissions measurement. Used for combustion efficiency calculations and emissions rate corrections.

attributes.name: pollutant_type
attributes.description: The type of pollutant measured in this reading. SO2 (Sulfur Dioxide), NOx (Nitrogen Oxides), CO2 (Carbon Dioxide), Hg (Mercury), PM (Particulate Matter), CO (Carbon Monoxide).

attributes.name: qa_certification_status
attributes.description: The quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) certification status of this emissions reading. Certified indicates the reading passed all QA/QC tests, provisional indicates temporary certification pending full testing, conditionally_valid indicates the reading is valid subject to conditions, invalid indicates the reading failed QA/QC, pending_certification indicates certification testing is in progress.

attributes.name: qa_test_date
attributes.description: The date when the most recent QA/QC certification test was performed on the CEMS monitor that recorded this reading. Used to verify data quality and compliance with EPA testing requirements.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this emissions reading record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this emissions reading record was last updated in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: reporting_period
attributes.description: The time period granularity for which this emissions reading is aggregated and reported to regulatory agencies. Hourly is the most granular level required by EPA Part 75.

attributes.name: reporting_quarter
attributes.description: The calendar quarter (1-4) in which this emissions reading occurred. Used for quarterly compliance reporting aggregation.

attributes.name: reporting_year
attributes.description: The calendar year in which this emissions reading occurred. Used for annual compliance reporting and allowance reconciliation.

attributes.name: stack_code
attributes.description: The unique identifier for the exhaust stack or flue where the CEMS monitor is installed and from which emissions are measured. A single stack may serve multiple generating units.

attributes.name: submitted_to_epa_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this emissions reading has been submitted to the EPA through the Emissions Collection and Monitoring Plan System (ECMPS). True if submitted, False if not yet submitted.

attributes.name: substitute_data_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this reading is substitute data rather than actual measured data. True if substitute data was used due to monitor downtime or failure, False if actual measured data. Substitute data is calculated using EPA-approved methodologies.

attributes.name: substitute_data_method
attributes.description: The EPA-approved methodology used to calculate substitute data when actual CEMS measurements are unavailable. Only populated when substitute_data_flag is True.

attributes.name: total_mass_emissions
attributes.description: The total mass of pollutant emitted during the measurement period, calculated from emission rate and operating time. Units are typically pounds (lbs) or tons depending on pollutant type and reporting requirements.

attributes.name: total_mass_emissions_unit
attributes.business_glossary_term: Total Mass Emissions Unit of Measure (UOM)
attributes.description: The unit of measure for total mass emissions. Common units include lbs (pounds), tons (short tons), kg (kilograms), metric_tons.

attributes.name: unit_type
attributes.description: The type of generating unit technology that produced this emissions reading. Used for emissions factor selection and compliance program applicability determination.

products.name: outage_event
products.description: Records of planned and unplanned generation outage events at the unit level. Captures outage start and end timestamps, outage type (forced, planned, maintenance, derating), capacity lost (MW), cause code (NERC GADS cause code), equipment component affected, responsible crew, estimated return-to-service date, actual return-to-service date, and NERC GADS reporting flag. Feeds NERC GADS submissions, generation availability analysis (EAF, EFOR), and IRP capacity planning. SSOT for generation unit outage history.
products.reference: NERC GADS (Generating Availability Data System) / IEEE 762

attributes.name: grid_reliability_event_id

attributes.name: grid_switching_order_id

attributes.name: impacted_distribution_substation_id

attributes.description: Identifier of the generation plant or facility where the outage occurred. Links to the plant asset registry.
