attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the parent substation that supplies this load zone. Links the zone to its source substation in the transmission-distribution interface.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network Data Model

attributes.name: forecast_zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.zone. Business justification: Distribution load zones are operational constructs that directly map to forecast zones for planning. Essential for integrated distribution planning, voltage optimization planning, and capacity studies

attributes.name: pnode_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.pnode. Business justification: Distribution load zones are mapped to transmission pnodes for LMP-based wholesale settlement, congestion cost allocation, and load forecasting in RTO/ISO markets. FERC settlement and distribution plan

attributes.description: FK to distribution.feeder.feeder_id — Load zones are associated with feeders. The description mentions 'associated feeders'. This is a many-to-many but the primary association is critical for load balancing operations.

attributes.name: service_territory_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.service_territory. Business justification: Load zones are logical groupings of network segments used for load balancing and DMS/ADMS operations — they exist within the geographic boundaries of a service territory. Adding service_territory_id t

attributes.name: capacity_mva
attributes.description: Total installed capacity of the load zone in megavolt-amperes, representing the maximum apparent power the zone infrastructure can support. Used for capacity planning and load transfer studies.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this load zone record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance, Utility Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: customer_count
attributes.description: Total number of customer premises served by this load zone. Used for reliability index calculations (SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI) and outage impact assessment.

attributes.name: der_penetration_mw
attributes.description: Total installed capacity of distributed energy resources (solar PV, wind, storage, etc.) within the load zone, measured in megawatts. Used for DER hosting capacity analysis and grid integration planning.

attributes.name: dms_zone_classification
attributes.description: Classification of the zone within the DMS/ADMS for automation capabilities. VVO-enabled zones support Volt-VAR Optimization, FLISR-enabled zones support Fault Location Isolation and Service Restoration, manual zones require operator intervention, hybrid zones have partial automation, and advanced zones support full ADMS integration.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when the load zone configuration became or will become effective. Used for tracking zone boundary changes, capacity upgrades, and operational transitions.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the load zone configuration expires or is scheduled for decommissioning. Null for active zones with no planned end date.

attributes.name: feeder_count
attributes.description: Number of distribution feeders associated with this load zone. Used for network topology analysis and load balancing.

attributes.name: flisr_enabled_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fault Location Isolation and Service Restoration (FLISR) Enabled Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether FLISR automation is enabled for this load zone. True means automated fault detection, isolation, and restoration; false means manual switching operations.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS Technical Documentation, IEEE 1547

attributes.name: geographic_boundary_wkt
attributes.description: Geographic boundary of the load zone represented as a WKT (Well-Known Text) polygon. Used for spatial analysis, outage mapping, and GIS integration with Esri ArcGIS Utility Network.
attributes.references: OGC Simple Features Specification, Esri ArcGIS Standards

attributes.name: hosting_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Maximum amount of additional DER capacity the zone can accommodate without infrastructure upgrades or operational issues, measured in megawatts. Used for interconnection screening and DER integration planning.

attributes.name: last_capacity_study_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent distribution capacity study performed for this load zone. Used to track planning cycle compliance and identify zones requiring updated analysis.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this load zone record was last updated. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization across systems.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance, Utility Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: load_profile_type
attributes.description: Dominant customer class or load profile characteristic of the zone. Residential zones peak in evening, commercial zones peak mid-day, industrial zones have steady load, mixed zones have diverse profiles, and agricultural zones have seasonal patterns.

attributes.name: next_capacity_study_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next distribution capacity study for this load zone. Used for planning resource allocation and ensuring regulatory compliance with capacity planning cycles.

attributes.name: nominal_load_mvar
attributes.description: Typical or average reactive power load of the zone under normal operating conditions, measured in megavolt-amperes reactive. Used for Volt-VAR optimization and power factor management.

attributes.name: nominal_load_mw
attributes.description: Typical or average real power load of the zone under normal operating conditions, measured in megawatts. Used for load balancing and capacity planning.

attributes.name: nominal_voltage_kv
attributes.description: Nominal operating voltage of the load zone in kilovolts. Typical distribution voltages range from 4.16 kV to 34.5 kV.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special considerations, or additional context about the load zone. May include information about unique load characteristics, planned projects, or operational constraints.

attributes.name: peak_demand_mw
attributes.description: Historical or forecasted peak real power demand for the zone, measured in megawatts. Critical for capacity planning and infrastructure investment decisions.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1, PUC Capacity Planning Requirements

attributes.name: peak_demand_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the peak demand was recorded or is forecasted to occur. Used for load profile analysis and demand response planning.

attributes.name: planning_area_code
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the broader distribution planning area or service territory that contains this load zone. Used for regional capacity planning and resource allocation.

attributes.name: power_factor_target
attributes.description: Target power factor for the load zone, typically between 0.95 and 1.00. Used for Volt-VAR optimization dispatch and capacitor bank control to minimize reactive power losses.

attributes.name: reliability_caidi_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI) Minutes
attributes.description: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index for the load zone, measured in minutes per interruption. Calculated as SAIDI/SAIFI. Indicates average restoration time. Key reliability metric reported to PUC.

attributes.name: reliability_saidi_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) Minutes
attributes.description: System Average Interruption Duration Index for the load zone, measured in minutes per customer per year. Key reliability metric reported to PUC. Lower values indicate better reliability.

attributes.name: reliability_saifi_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) Count
attributes.description: System Average Interruption Frequency Index for the load zone, measured as number of interruptions per customer per year. Key reliability metric reported to PUC. Lower values indicate better reliability.

attributes.name: scada_integration_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Integration Status
attributes.description: Level of SCADA system integration for real-time monitoring and control of the load zone. Fully integrated zones have complete telemetry and control, partially integrated zones have limited coverage, not integrated zones rely on manual operations, and planned zones are scheduled for integration.
attributes.references: NERC CIP Standards, OSIsoft PI Integration Standards

attributes.name: utilization_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of peak demand to installed capacity, indicating how heavily the zone infrastructure is utilized. Values approaching 1.0 indicate need for capacity expansion.

attributes.name: voltage_regulation_target_max_pu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Voltage Regulation Target Maximum Per Unit (pu)
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable voltage level for the zone expressed in per-unit (pu) of nominal voltage. Typically 1.05 pu per ANSI C84.1 Range A. Used by VVO algorithms to maintain voltage within acceptable limits.

attributes.name: voltage_regulation_target_min_pu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Voltage Regulation Target Minimum Per Unit (pu)
attributes.description: Minimum acceptable voltage level for the zone expressed in per-unit (pu) of nominal voltage. Typically 0.95 pu per ANSI C84.1 Range A. Used by VVO algorithms to maintain voltage within acceptable limits.

attributes.name: vvo_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether Volt-VAR Optimization is enabled for this load zone. True means VVO algorithms actively control voltage and reactive power devices; false means manual or legacy control.

attributes.name: zone_code
attributes.description: Business identifier for the load zone, typically a human-readable alphanumeric code used in operational systems and dispatch communications. Externally known identifier for the zone.

attributes.name: zone_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the load zone, often reflecting geographic area or substation association (e.g., 'Downtown West Zone', 'Substation 5 North').

attributes.name: zone_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the load zone. Active zones are in service, inactive zones are temporarily out of service, planned zones are under construction, decommissioned zones are retired, and maintenance zones are undergoing scheduled work.

attributes.name: zone_type
attributes.description: Classification of the load zone based on its role in the distribution network hierarchy. Primary zones serve major load centers, secondary zones serve neighborhood clusters, tertiary zones serve smaller segments, and special zones serve unique loads (industrial parks, critical infrastructure).

products.name: distribution_switching_order
products.description: Transactional record capturing planned and emergency switching operations on the distribution network, including the full sequence of individual switching steps. Captures switching order number, order type (planned/emergency/FLISR-automated/load-transfer), initiating event reference, crew assignment, authorization approvals, safety clearances, and completion status. Each order contains an ordered sequence of switching steps, each with: step sequence number, target device, operation type (open/close/tag/untag), required pre/post device state, execution timestamp, operator ID, confirmed device state, and step completion status. Records pre-switch and post-switch network topology for each order. SSOT for all distribution switching operations including FLISR-automated sequences, load transfer operations, and step-level audit trail. Sourced from GE PowerOn ADMS switching management module.
products.reference: GE PowerOn ADMS Switching Management / IEEE 1547

attributes.name: load_transferred_kw

attributes.name: major_event_exclusion_flag

attributes.name: operator_override_flag

attributes.name: puc_reportable_flag

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this FLISR event record was last modified in the data system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: restoration_devices_operated

attributes.name: restoration_time_seconds
attributes.description: Elapsed time in seconds from fault detection to completion of FLISR restoration switching sequence. Critical metric for CAIDI calculation and FLISR performance benchmarking.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: saidi_contribution_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) Contribution in Minutes
attributes.description: Calculated contribution of this FLISR event to the SAIDI reliability index, in customer-minutes. Computed as (customers affected × duration) / total customers served. Critical for PUC reliability reporting.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: saifi_contribution
attributes.business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) Contribution
attributes.description: Calculated contribution of this FLISR event to the SAIFI reliability index. Computed as customers affected / total customers served. Critical for PUC reliability reporting.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: scada_alarm_count

attributes.name: storm_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the storm event record if this reliability event was part of a larger storm or weather system. Enables storm-level reliability aggregation and mutual aid analysis.

attributes.name: transformer_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.transformer. Business justification: Distribution reliability interruption events are frequently caused by transformer failures (overloads, insulation failures, oil leaks, lightning strikes). The distribution_reliability_event already li

attributes.name: violation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.violation. Business justification: A distribution reliability event exceeding regulatory duration or frequency thresholds directly triggers a compliance violation. Utilities track which outage events resulted in PUC violations for pena

attributes.name: weather_input_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.weather_input. Business justification: Reliability events are correlated with weather forecast inputs for IEEE 1366 major event day classification, storm hardening analysis, and PUC regulatory reporting. weather_condition is a denormalized

attributes.name: crew_arrival_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when field crew arrived at the fault location. Used to calculate crew travel time and on-site restoration duration.

attributes.name: crew_dispatch_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when field crew was dispatched to investigate and repair the fault. Used to calculate crew response time and restoration performance metrics.

attributes.name: critical_customer_affected_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether any critical customers (hospitals, emergency services, water treatment, etc.) were affected by the interruption. Used for priority restoration and regulatory notification.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS Critical Customer Management

attributes.name: customer_minutes_interrupted
attributes.description: Total customer-minutes of interruption calculated as customers_interrupted × duration_minutes. Used to calculate SAIDI (System Average Interruption Duration Index) per IEEE 1366.

attributes.name: customers_interrupted
attributes.description: Total number of customer accounts experiencing service interruption during this event. Used to calculate SAIFI (System Average Interruption Frequency Index) per IEEE 1366.

attributes.name: customers_restored_by_flisr
attributes.description: Number of customers automatically restored by FLISR automation without manual crew intervention. Used to quantify FLISR benefit and avoided customer-minutes interrupted.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system that originated this reliability event record (e.g., GE PowerOn ADMS, OSIsoft PI, SAP IS-U). Used for data lineage and source system reconciliation.

attributes.name: duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the interruption event in minutes, calculated as the difference between restoration_timestamp and event_start_timestamp. Used for IEEE 1366 sustained vs. momentary classification.

attributes.name: energy_not_served_mwh
attributes.description: Total energy not delivered to customers in megawatt-hours (MWh) due to the interruption, calculated as load_interrupted_mw × duration_hours. Used for economic impact analysis and PUC reporting.

attributes.name: equipment_age_years
attributes.description: Age in years of the failed equipment at the time of the event. Used for asset health correlation and age-based replacement program justification.

attributes.name: equipment_failed
attributes.description: Type of distribution equipment that failed and caused the interruption (e.g., transformer, conductor, insulator, pole, underground cable). Used for asset failure analysis and replacement prioritization.

attributes.name: estimated_restoration_time
attributes.description: Initial estimated time of restoration communicated to customers and regulators when the event began. Used to measure ERT accuracy and customer communication effectiveness.

attributes.name: event_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the reliability event, typically generated by the Outage Management System (OMS) or Advanced Distribution Management System (ADMS). Used for external reporting and cross-system correlation.

attributes.name: event_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the reliability event began (first customer interruption detected). Captured from SCADA, AMI, or customer call-in data via OMS/ADMS.

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Classification of the interruption event per IEEE 1366 definitions: sustained (>5 minutes), momentary (≤5 minutes), or planned (scheduled maintenance outage).

attributes.name: exclusion_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why the event is excluded from IEEE 1366 reliability index calculations, if ieee_1366_exclusion_flag is true. References specific IEEE 1366 exclusion criteria.

attributes.name: fault_latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the fault location in decimal degrees. Used for spatial reliability analysis and vegetation management correlation.

attributes.name: fault_location_description
attributes.description: Textual description of the physical location where the fault occurred (e.g., street address, pole number, landmark). Used for crew dispatch and asset maintenance correlation.

attributes.name: fault_longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the fault location in decimal degrees. Used for spatial reliability analysis and vegetation management correlation.

attributes.name: flisr_operated_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fault Location Isolation and Service Restoration (FLISR) Operated Flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether FLISR automation successfully operated to isolate the fault and restore service to unaffected customers. Used to measure FLISR effectiveness and MAIFI (Momentary Average Interruption Frequency Index) reduction.

attributes.name: flisr_operation_time_seconds
attributes.description: Time in seconds for FLISR automation to isolate the fault and restore service to unaffected segments. Used to measure FLISR performance and reduction in customer-minutes interrupted.

attributes.name: ieee_1366_exclusion_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this event should be excluded from IEEE 1366 reliability index calculations per standard exclusion criteria (e.g., loss of supply, prearranged interruption, customer-owned equipment failure).

attributes.name: load_interrupted_mw
attributes.description: Total electrical load in megawatts (MW) interrupted during the event, captured from SCADA or estimated from customer count and load profiles. Used for energy not served (ENS) calculations.

attributes.name: major_event_day_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this event occurred on a Major Event Day per IEEE 1366 2.5-beta method. Major Event Days are excluded from annual reliability index calculations to prevent catastrophic events from skewing performance metrics.

attributes.name: protective_device_type
attributes.description: Type of protective device that operated to isolate the fault (e.g., recloser, circuit breaker, fuse, sectionalizer). Used for protective device performance analysis and coordination studies.

attributes.name: puc_report_date
attributes.description: Date when the reliability event was reported to the Public Utility Commission, if puc_reportable_flag is true. Used to track regulatory reporting compliance.

attributes.name: puc_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this event must be reported to the state Public Utility Commission per regulatory requirements. Typically true for sustained interruptions affecting a threshold number of customers.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this reliability event record was first created in the data warehouse. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this reliability event record was last modified. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: repair_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the repair work performed by field crew to restore service, including equipment replaced, temporary repairs, or permanent fixes.

attributes.name: restoration_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when service was fully restored to all affected customers. Used to calculate event duration and customer-minutes interrupted.

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the distribution circuit affected by the event (e.g., 12.47, 13.2, 34.5). Used for voltage-class reliability analysis.

products.name: feeder_load_reading
products.description: Transactional record for interval load measurements at feeder head and key monitoring points on the distribution network, sourced from SCADA/OSIsoft PI historian or similar data historian. Captures reading timestamp, feeder or segment identifier, measurement point type (feeder head/midpoint/tie point), active power (MW), reactive power (MVAr), apparent power (MVA), current (A per phase), voltage (kV per phase), power factor, temperature, and data quality flag. SSOT for distribution-level load telemetry distinct from AMI meter interval data owned by the metering domain. Supports load balancing, capacity planning, peak demand analysis, volt-VAR optimization feedback, and normal/emergency rating calculations.
products.reference: OSIsoft PI Historian / SCADA ICCP / IEC 61968 MDM

attributes.name: feeder_load_reading_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the feeder load reading record. Primary key for this transactional measurement event.

attributes.name: ems_node_id

attributes.name: event_id
attributes.description: Identifier linking this reading to an outage event if the reading was captured during or immediately after an outage. Null if no outage was active at reading time.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Outage Management System; OMS Event Registry

attributes.name: flisr_event_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: FLISR (Fault Location, Isolation, and Service Restoration) Event ID
attributes.description: Identifier linking this reading to a FLISR automation event if the reading was captured during an automated switching sequence. Null if no FLISR event was active.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - FLISR Module; IEEE 1547.4 Islanding Standard

attributes.name: forecast_model_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.model. Business justification: Feeder load readings are used to validate and calibrate forecast models — the accuracy assessment process (MAPE, RMSE tracking) requires linking actual feeder readings to the specific forecast model t

attributes.name: load_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to forecast.load. Business justification: Actual feeder load readings must be compared against load forecasts for accuracy measurement and model calibration. Essential for forecast accuracy tracking, MAPE calculation, model validation, and co

attributes.name: load_zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.load_zone. Business justification: Feeder load readings are the primary data source for load zone demand analysis, load balancing, and DMS/ADMS state estimation. Load zones are logical groupings of network segments used for load balanc

attributes.name: meter_point_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the specific monitoring point on the feeder where the reading was captured (e.g., feeder head, midpoint sensor, tie point). Corresponds to SCADA tag or PI point identifier.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI - Point Configuration; SCADA Tag Registry

attributes.name: planned_outage_window_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to outage.planned_outage_window. Linking feeder load readings to planned outage windows supports work manag

attributes.name: primary_feeder_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution feeder or circuit segment where the load measurement was taken. Links to the feeder asset in the distribution network topology.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Feeder Registry; Esri ArcGIS Utility Network

attributes.name: scada_point_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.scada_point. Business justification: Feeder load readings are sourced from SCADA telemetry points. Linking to the source scada_point enables data lineage traceability, SCADA data quality validation, and PI historian tag reconciliation re

attributes.name: storm_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to outage.storm_event. Business justification: Feeder load readings during storm events are essential for post-storm load restoration sequencing, storm cost estimation, and NERC reportable event analysis. Linking load readings to storm events enab

attributes.name: tertiary_feeder_id
attributes.description: FK to distribution.feeder.feeder_id — Feeder load readings are measurements taken at feeder head or monitoring points. The feeder FK is essential for associating readings with the correct feeder for load analysis and capacity planning.

attributes.name: active_power_mw
attributes.description: Real power measured in megawatts (MW) at the monitoring point. Represents the actual power flowing through the feeder segment at the reading timestamp. Used for load balancing and capacity planning.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Power Definitions; NERC MOD Standards

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_celsius
attributes.description: Ambient temperature in degrees Celsius at or near the monitoring point. Used for thermal rating adjustments and equipment derating calculations under high-temperature conditions.
attributes.references: IEEE 738 - Conductor Thermal Rating; NERC FAC Standards

attributes.name: apparent_power_mva
attributes.description: Apparent power measured in megavolt-amperes (MVA) at the monitoring point. Represents the total power (vector sum of active and reactive power) and is used for equipment rating and capacity calculations.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Power Definitions; ANSI C84.1 Voltage Standard

attributes.name: current_phase_a_amperes
attributes.description: Current measured on Phase A conductor in amperes at the monitoring point. Used for load balancing across phases and thermal limit monitoring.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.118 - Synchrophasor Measurements; ANSI C84.1

attributes.name: current_phase_b_amperes
attributes.description: Current measured on Phase B conductor in amperes at the monitoring point. Used for load balancing across phases and thermal limit monitoring.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.118 - Synchrophasor Measurements; ANSI C84.1

attributes.name: current_phase_c_amperes
attributes.description: Current measured on Phase C conductor in amperes at the monitoring point. Used for load balancing across phases and thermal limit monitoring.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.118 - Synchrophasor Measurements; ANSI C84.1

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Quality indicator for the reading. Good indicates validated data; suspect indicates data outside normal range but not rejected; bad indicates failed validation; estimated indicates imputed value; missing indicates no data received. Aligns with VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) processes.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI - Data Quality Attributes; Oracle Utilities MDM VEE Rules

attributes.name: data_retention_category
attributes.description: Classification determining the retention period for this reading. Operational (1-2 years); regulatory (5-7 years per FERC/PUC requirements); historical (10+ years for trend analysis); archive (permanent retention for critical events).
attributes.references: FERC Data Retention Requirements; State PUC Regulations; SOX Compliance

attributes.name: data_source_type
attributes.description: Classification of the data acquisition method. SCADA realtime indicates live telemetry; historian archive indicates retrieved from PI or similar historian; manual entry indicates operator-entered value; estimated indicates calculated/imputed value.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI - Data Source Classification; Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: der_generation_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether DER generation (solar, wind, battery storage) was active on this feeder segment at the time of reading. Used for DER impact analysis and reverse power flow detection.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547 - DER Interconnection; DERMS Integration Standards

attributes.name: emergency_rating_mva
attributes.description: Emergency short-term thermal rating of the feeder segment in MVA. Represents the maximum load that can be carried for a limited duration (typically 15 minutes to 4 hours) during contingency conditions.
attributes.references: IEEE 738 - Conductor Thermal Rating; NERC FAC-008 Facility Ratings

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Method used to estimate the reading value if actual data was missing or invalid. None indicates no estimation was performed; other values indicate the specific estimation algorithm applied per MDM VEE rules.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Estimation Rules; Industry Best Practices

attributes.name: frequency_hz
attributes.description: System frequency measured in hertz at the monitoring point. Nominal value is 60 Hz in North America; deviations indicate grid stability issues and are monitored per NERC reliability standards.
attributes.references: NERC BAL Standards; IEEE C37.118 Synchrophasor Standard

attributes.name: loading_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of normal rating currently being utilized, calculated as (apparent_power_mva / normal_rating_mva) * 100. Key metric for capacity planning and identifying overloaded feeders.
attributes.references: NERC MOD Standards; Utility Capacity Planning Guidelines

attributes.name: measurement_point_type
attributes.description: Classification of the monitoring location on the distribution network. Feeder head represents the substation exit point; midpoint and tie point represent intermediate monitoring locations; recloser, capacitor bank, and regulator represent device-level monitoring points.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS - Network Topology Model; IEEE 1547 DER Interconnection Standard

attributes.name: normal_rating_mva
attributes.description: Normal continuous thermal rating of the feeder segment in MVA under standard ambient conditions. Used to calculate loading percentage and identify overload conditions.
attributes.references: IEEE 738 - Conductor Thermal Rating; NERC FAC-008 Facility Ratings

attributes.name: peak_demand_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether this reading occurred during a system peak demand period. Used for peak demand analysis and capacity planning studies.
attributes.references: Utility Load Forecasting Standards; PUC Peak Demand Reporting

attributes.name: pi_point_name
attributes.description: OSIsoft PI point tag name or equivalent historian tag identifier for this measurement. Provides traceability back to the source SCADA tag in the historian system.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI - Tag Naming Convention; SCADA Integration Standards

attributes.name: power_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of active power to apparent power (dimensionless, range -1.0 to +1.0). Indicates the efficiency of power delivery and is a key input for volt-VAR optimization and capacitor bank control.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Power Definitions; Utility Tariff Power Factor Requirements

attributes.name: reactive_power_mvar
attributes.description: Reactive power measured in megavolt-amperes reactive (MVAr) at the monitoring point. Critical for volt-VAR optimization and power factor management on the distribution network.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Power Definitions; NERC VAR Standards

attributes.name: reading_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the load measurement was recorded by the SCADA system or data historian. Represents the actual event time of the observation, distinct from record creation time.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI - Event Timestamp; IEEE C37.118 Synchrophasor Standard

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this record was first inserted into the lakehouse silver layer. Distinct from reading_timestamp which represents the actual measurement event time. Used for data lineage and audit trail.
attributes.references: Data Governance - Audit Trail Standards; Databricks Lakehouse Best Practices

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this record was last modified in the lakehouse silver layer. Updated when VEE processes revise data quality flags or estimation values. Used for change tracking and audit trail.
attributes.references: Data Governance - Audit Trail Standards; Databricks Lakehouse Best Practices

attributes.name: reverse_power_flow_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether power was flowing in the reverse direction (from customer premises back to substation) at the time of reading. Indicates high DER penetration or net export conditions.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547 - DER Interconnection; Distribution Grid Modernization Standards

attributes.name: scada_source_system
attributes.business_glossary_term: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) Source System
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the SCADA system or data historian that originated this reading (e.g., OSIsoft PI, GE iFIX, Schneider ClearSCADA). Used for data lineage and troubleshooting.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI - System Configuration; GE PowerOn ADMS Integration

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Status of the VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) process for this reading. Validated indicates the reading passed all quality checks; pending indicates awaiting validation; failed indicates rejected by validation rules; bypassed indicates validation was skipped.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Engine; NERC Data Quality Standards

attributes.name: voltage_phase_a_kv
attributes.description: Voltage measured on Phase A in kilovolts at the monitoring point. Critical for voltage regulation and ANSI C84.1 compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ANSI C84.1 - Voltage Ratings; IEEE 1547 DER Standard

attributes.name: voltage_phase_b_kv
attributes.description: Voltage measured on Phase B in kilovolts at the monitoring point. Critical for voltage regulation and ANSI C84.1 compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ANSI C84.1 - Voltage Ratings; IEEE 1547 DER Standard

attributes.name: voltage_phase_c_kv
attributes.description: Voltage measured on Phase C in kilovolts at the monitoring point. Critical for voltage regulation and ANSI C84.1 compliance monitoring.
attributes.references: ANSI C84.1 - Voltage Ratings; IEEE 1547 DER Standard

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: General weather condition at the time of reading. Used for correlating load patterns with weather events and for storm impact analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: clear|cloudy|rain|snow|storm|extreme_heat|extreme_cold — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

products.name: der_interconnection_point
products.description: Master record for the physical point of interconnection (POI) where a Distributed Energy Resource connects to the distribution network. Captures POI identifier, DER type (solar PV/battery/EV charger/CHP/wind), nameplate capacity (kW), inverter type and settings, interconnection voltage level, feeder and segment assignment, GIS location, NEM eligibility, anti-islanding protection scheme, DERMS reference, IEEE 1547 compliance status, and interconnection agreement status. SSOT for DER physical connection points on the distribution network. Supports hosting capacity analysis, DERMS integration, reverse power flow monitoring, and state interconnection rule compliance (e.g., Rule 21, SB 700).

attributes.name: derms_device_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS) Device Identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this DER in the DERMS platform. Used for real-time monitoring, dispatch commands, and aggregation into virtual power plants.

attributes.name: derms_integration_enabled
attributes.business_glossary_term: Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS) Integration Enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether this DER is integrated with the utility DERMS for monitoring and control. True enables participation in demand response, VPP aggregation, and grid services programs.

attributes.name: export_capacity_kw
attributes.description: Maximum power the DER is authorized to export to the distribution grid in kilowatts. May be less than nameplate capacity due to interconnection agreement limits or hosting capacity constraints.

attributes.name: export_limit_control_method

attributes.name: frequency_watt_control_enabled

attributes.name: gis_feature_code

attributes.name: hosting_capacity_impact_mw

attributes.name: ieee_1547_category

attributes.name: ieee_1547_compliance_status

attributes.name: interconnection_application_date

attributes.name: interconnection_approval_date

products.name: switching_step
products.description: This association product represents the atomic operational unit of a distribution switching order - each individual device operation performed as part of a switching sequence. It captures the step-by-step execution of switching orders on sectionalizing devices, including operation type, device state transitions, timing, operator confirmation, and step completion status. Each record links one switching order to one sectionalizing device operation with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific switching action. Critical for NERC CIP compliance, safety clearance tracking, FLISR automation audit trails, and post-event analysis.. Existence Justification: In distribution operations, a switching order executes a sequence of individual device operations (switching steps), where each step operates on one sectionalizing device. One switching order operates on multiple devices in sequence (e.g., open recloser A, close switch B, open fuse C), and one device is operated on by many different switching orders over time (planned maintenance, emergency restoration, FLISR automation). The switching step is the atomic operational unit tracked for NERC CIP compliance, safety clearance, and audit trails.

Manages meter-to-cash data flow, MDM integration via Oracle Utilities MDM, and raw/validated interval data streams feeding billing, demand response, and grid operations domains.

products.name: meter
products.description: Master record for every physical metering device deployed or managed by the utility — smart meters (AMI), interval meters, demand meters, and legacy electromechanical units. Captures device identity (serial number, manufacturer, model), firmware version, meter form factor, voltage class, current rating, number of elements, register configuration, seal status, and AMI head-end system assignment. Includes embedded communication module attributes: module type (RF mesh/PLC/cellular), module serial number, MAC/IP address, signal strength baseline, module firmware version, communication protocol, assigned AMI network segment, and module status — supporting independent module replacement tracking without a separate entity. Also captures the active and historical programmed operational configuration: interval length setting (15/30/60 min), TOU rate program assignment, demand reset interval, load profile channels enabled, remote disconnect/reconnect capability, and configuration effective dates for versioning. SSOT for meter asset identity, communication endpoint, and device configuration within the metering domain; links to the asset domain for full lifecycle management.

attributes.name: data_quality_score

attributes.name: der_capacity_kw

attributes.name: der_interconnection_flag

attributes.name: gps_longitude

attributes.name: interval_length_minutes

attributes.name: last_meter_reading_date

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.references: SOX Internal Controls - Data Audit Standards

attributes.name: load_profile_class
attributes.description: Customer segment classification determining consumption patterns, rate structures, and demand response eligibility. Critical for load forecasting and grid planning.

attributes.name: net_metering_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether net energy metering is enabled for this service point due to behind-the-meter generation (solar, wind, CHP).

attributes.name: network_topology_node
attributes.description: Logical node identifier in the electrical network topology model. Used by ADMS and DMS systems for network analysis and switching operations.

attributes.name: peak_demand_kw
attributes.description: Maximum recorded demand in kilowatts at this meter point. Used for capacity planning, rate design, and demand charge billing.

attributes.name: phase_configuration
attributes.description: Electrical phase configuration of the service connection. Determines metering channel requirements and load balancing considerations.

attributes.name: service_activation_date

attributes.name: service_deactivation_date
attributes.description: Date when service was permanently deactivated at this meter point. Null for active service points.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Service Point Lifecycle

attributes.name: service_point_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the meter point. Active indicates the point is in service and generating consumption data.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Service Point Lifecycle

attributes.name: service_point_type
attributes.description: Classification of the commodity delivered at this meter point. Determines applicable rate schedules and measurement requirements.

attributes.name: service_voltage_level
attributes.description: Voltage classification at which energy is delivered to this meter point. Determines metering accuracy requirements and applicable tariffs.

attributes.name: service_voltage_value
attributes.description: Nominal voltage in volts at which service is delivered (e.g., 120V, 240V, 480V, 13.8kV). Used for power quality monitoring and equipment compatibility verification.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the authoritative source system for this meter point record. Supports multi-system data integration and master data governance.

attributes.name: tou_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether time-of-use rate pricing is active for this meter point. Requires interval data collection and TOU-capable metering.

attributes.name: vee_processing_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: VEE (Validation Estimation and Editing) Processing Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether meter data from this point undergoes VEE processing for data quality assurance before billing and analytics.

products.name: meter_installation
products.description: Tracks the active and historical association between a meter device and a meter point — the physical installation record. Captures installation date, removal date, meter reading at installation (start index), meter reading at removal (end index), installation technician, seal numbers applied, multiplier/CT ratio in effect, and installation status. Enables meter-to-premise traceability for billing, VEE, and regulatory audit. Supports meter swap history and back-billing calculations.

attributes.name: billing_end_date

attributes.name: billing_start_date

products.name: interval_reading
products.description: Raw interval energy consumption and demand data collected from AMI smart meters at sub-hourly or hourly granularity (typically 15-min or 60-min intervals). Stores channel identifier, interval start timestamp, interval end timestamp, raw kWh or kW value, quality code (raw/estimated/substituted), data collection method (AMI push, manual, estimated), head-end system receipt timestamp, and collection run reference. This is the foundational time-series dataset feeding Oracle Utilities MDM VEE processing, billing, demand response, and grid operations. Immutable raw record — validated versions are stored in validated_interval_reading. High-volume transactional entity; typical utility processes millions of interval records daily.
products.reference: Oracle Utilities MDM — Interval Data / ANSI C12.19 Interval Data Table

attributes.name: net_metering_flag

attributes.name: received_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the interval reading was received by the head-end system or MDM platform. Used for latency analysis and data freshness monitoring. Distinct from the interval measurement time.

attributes.name: reprocessing_flag

attributes.name: reverse_flow_flag

attributes.name: time_zone_offset

products.name: meter_read
products.description: Scalar (register-level) meter reading record and associated read scheduling — capturing both the cumulative register value at a specific point in time and the recurring schedule governing when reads are collected. For readings: stores read date, read time, register identifier, read value, read type (scheduled/special/final/initial), read source (AMR/AMI/manual/estimated), reader employee reference, and read quality flag. For scheduling: defines read cycle (monthly/bi-monthly/daily), read method (AMI automated/manual route), scheduled read date, route assignment, billing cycle alignment, schedule code, and active status. Drives field crew routing for manual reads and AMI polling schedules for automated collection. Feeds billing domain consumption calculation. Distinct from interval_reading (which is time-series) — this is the periodic scalar snapshot and its collection governance.
products.reference: SAP IS-U — Meter Reading / Oracle CC&B — Meter Read
