attributes.name: meter_reading_route_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.meter_reading_route. Business justification: A scalar meter read is collected as part of a specific meter reading route execution. meter_read currently carries read_cycle_code (STRING) which is a denormalized reference to the route — this maps t

attributes.name: nem_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to renewable.nem_account. Business justification: NEM billing requires meter reads to be directly associated with the NEM account for true-up calculations and export credit determination. Enables direct NEM billing reconciliation without joining thro

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: State PUC rules impose compliance obligations on meter reading frequency, estimated read limits, and read methodology. Linking meter_read to the governing obligation enables compliance reporting on es

attributes.name: outage_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to outage.event. Business justification: Meter reads flagged with power_outage_flag must be linked to the specific outage event for billing adjustment processing, VEE exception investigation, and NERC/PUC regulatory reporting of energy-not-s

attributes.name: premise_id
attributes.description: Reference to the service premise where the meter is installed. Enables geographic and customer aggregation of reads.

attributes.name: primary_meter_point_id
attributes.description: Reference to the logical service point (delivery point) associated with this meter read. Used for billing and consumption analysis.

attributes.name: rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the rate schedule (tariff) in effect for this service point at the time of the read. Used to determine Time-of-Use (TOU) periods, Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) applicability, and billing determinants.

attributes.name: register_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific register on the meter (e.g., kWh delivered, kWh received, kVArh). Multi-register meters have multiple read records per read event.

attributes.name: to_meter_point_id
attributes.description: FK to metering.meter_point.meter_point_id — Scalar meter reads must reference the meter point where the read was taken. Essential for billing cycle consumption calculation.

attributes.name: vee_rule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) rule that processed this read. Links to the validation rule configuration for audit and troubleshooting.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Rule Engine

attributes.name: average_daily_usage
attributes.description: Consumption divided by consumption days. Expressed in kWh per day or MWh per day. Used for customer usage profiling, demand response eligibility, and anomaly detection.

attributes.name: billed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this meter read has been used in a billing run and invoice generation. True if billed; False if pending or unbilled. Used to prevent duplicate billing and support billing cycle reconciliation.

attributes.name: consumption_days
attributes.description: Number of days between the current read date and the previous read date. Used to normalize consumption for billing and to calculate average daily usage.

attributes.name: consumption_kwh
attributes.description: Calculated energy consumption for the period (current read value minus previous read value). Expressed in kilowatt-hours (kWh) or megawatt-hours (MWh). This is the billable quantity fed to the billing domain.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this meter read record was first created in the MDM (Meter Data Management) system. Used for data lineage and audit trails.

attributes.name: demand_kw
attributes.description: Peak demand recorded during the read period, expressed in kilowatts (kW) or megawatts (MW). Captured for commercial and industrial customers on demand-based rate schedules. Null for residential meters without demand registers.

attributes.name: demand_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the peak demand occurred during the read period. Used for Time-of-Use (TOU) and Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) rate application.

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Algorithm or rule used to estimate the read value when actual read was unavailable. Examples: HIST_AVG (historical average), PREV_YEAR (same period prior year), PRO_RATA (prorated from partial period), ADL (average daily load). Null for actual reads.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Estimation Rules

attributes.name: exception_code
attributes.description: Code identifying any exception or anomaly detected during read capture or validation. Examples: HIGH_USAGE, LOW_USAGE, ZERO_CONSUMPTION, NEGATIVE_CONSUMPTION, TAMPER, COMM_FAILURE. Used to trigger investigation workflows.

attributes.name: multiplier
attributes.description: Constant multiplier applied to the raw register reading to calculate actual consumption. Used for current transformer (CT) and potential transformer (PT) ratios on high-voltage meters. Default is 1.0 for direct-connected meters.

attributes.name: previous_read_date
attributes.description: Date of the prior valid read for this register. Used to calculate the consumption period length (days between reads) and validate read sequence.

attributes.name: previous_read_value
attributes.description: The register value from the prior valid read. Used to calculate consumption (current read minus previous read) and detect anomalies such as reverse flow or register rollover.

attributes.name: read_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the meter reading was captured. Principal business event timestamp for billing cycle alignment and consumption period determination.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ-015 - Meter Reading Business Practices

attributes.name: read_frequency
attributes.description: The recurring interval at which reads are scheduled for this meter. Monthly: standard residential. Bi-monthly: some residential jurisdictions. Daily: large commercial/industrial or AMI. On-demand: special reads only.

attributes.name: read_method
attributes.description: Technical method used to capture the reading. Optical: infrared port. RF: radio frequency. PLC: power line carrier. Cellular: mobile network. Visual: technician reads display. Handheld: portable reader device.

attributes.name: read_quality_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the quality or exception condition of the read. Examples: OK (normal), EST (estimated), REV (reverse flow), OVF (overflow), PWR (power outage), TMR (tamper detected). Aligns with ANSI C12.19 quality flags.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.19 - Event Log and Quality Flags

attributes.name: read_reason_code
attributes.description: Business reason for the read event. Examples: BILL (billing cycle), MOVE (move-in/move-out), DISC (disconnect), RECON (reconnect), INSP (inspection), COMP (complaint investigation). Used for operational reporting and audit.

attributes.name: read_sequence_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the meter read, often formatted as meter number plus read date. Used for external reference and audit trails.

attributes.name: read_source
attributes.description: Method by which the reading was obtained. AMI: Advanced Metering Infrastructure (two-way automated). AMR: Automated Meter Reading (one-way drive-by). Manual: field technician on-site. Estimated: calculated by VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) process. Customer: self-reported. Remote: handheld or mobile device.
attributes.references: NAESB RMR - Retail Meter Reading Standards

attributes.name: read_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the meter read. Valid: passed VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) and accepted for billing. Estimated: calculated value pending actual read. Suspect: flagged for review. Failed: read attempt unsuccessful. Pending_validation: awaiting VEE processing. Corrected: replaced by subsequent correction read.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Status Workflow

attributes.name: read_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the meter reading was captured, including time zone. Used for interval boundary alignment and AMI (Advanced Metering Infrastructure) event correlation.

attributes.name: read_type
attributes.description: Classification of the read event. Scheduled: routine billing cycle read. Special: off-cycle read for move-in/move-out or investigation. Final: account closure. Initial: new service activation. Test: commissioning or validation. Correction: replacement of erroneous prior read.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - Read Type Classification

attributes.name: read_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the read value. Common values: kWh (kilowatt-hour), MWh (megawatt-hour), kVArh (kilovolt-ampere reactive hour) for electric; CCF, MCF, Therms for gas; Gallons for water. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: kWh|MWh|kVArh|MVArh|kW|MW|kVA|MVA|CCF|MCF|Therms|Gallons — 12 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ-015 - Unit of Measure Standards

attributes.name: read_value
attributes.description: The cumulative register value captured at the read timestamp. For energy meters, typically kilowatt-hours (kWh) or megawatt-hours (MWh). This is the raw scalar reading before consumption calculation.
attributes.references: ANSI C12.19 - Utility Industry End Device Data Tables

attributes.name: register_digits
attributes.description: Number of digits on the meter register display. Used to detect register rollover (e.g., a 5-digit register rolls from 99999 to 00000). Typical values: 5, 6, 7.

attributes.name: register_rollover_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the register rolled over during this read period (current read value is less than previous read value due to register capacity limit). True if rollover detected; False otherwise.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Rollover Detection

attributes.name: scheduled_read_date
attributes.description: The planned date for this meter read as defined by the read schedule. Used to measure on-time read performance and identify late or early reads.

attributes.name: tou_period
attributes.description: The TOU rate period for this register reading. On-peak: highest rate hours. Off-peak: lowest rate hours. Shoulder: mid-tier hours. Super-off-peak: ultra-low rate hours (e.g., overnight EV charging). Null for non-TOU registers.

attributes.name: tou_register_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this register captures Time-of-Use (TOU) segmented consumption (e.g., on-peak, off-peak, shoulder). True for TOU registers; False for cumulative registers. TOU meters have multiple read records per read event.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this meter read record was last modified. Tracks VEE corrections, status changes, and data quality improvements.

products.name: vee_rule
products.description: Defines the business rules applied during the VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) process in Oracle Utilities MDM. Each rule specifies the rule type (validation/estimation/editing), rule algorithm, threshold parameters (e.g., spike tolerance percentage, zero-consumption threshold), applicable meter types, priority order, effective date range, and regulatory basis. Governs data quality for billing-quality interval data. Reference entity managed by the metering operations team.
products.reference: Oracle Utilities MDM — VEE Rule Configuration

attributes.name: vee_rule_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Rule Identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the VEE rule. Primary key for the VEE rule reference entity.

attributes.name: asset_class_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.class. Business justification: VEE validation rules apply to specific meter asset classes (e.g., different estimation methods for residential vs. industrial CT meters). asset.class is the authoritative meter classification taxonomy

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: VEE rules implement regulatory obligations for data quality, estimation limits, validation thresholds mandated by state PUC orders. Enables compliance mapping, regulatory justification for VEE algorit

attributes.name: rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.rate_schedule. Business justification: VEE rules are scoped to specific rate schedules (TOU validation rules apply only to TOU rate schedules). The plain applicable_rate_schedules column on vee_rule is a denormalization signal. This FK ena

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Business justification: VEE rules implementing FERC Order 676 or state PUC data quality standards are established through regulatory filings. vee_rule has regulatory_basis (plain text denormalization). Replacing with regulat

attributes.name: algorithm_type
attributes.description: The computational algorithm or method used by the rule to validate, estimate, or edit meter data (e.g., threshold-based, statistical analysis, linear regression, interpolation). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: threshold|statistical|regression|interpolation|substitution|comparison|pattern_matching — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: applicable_service_types
attributes.description: Type of utility service to which this VEE rule applies (electric, gas, water, steam). Ensures rules are applied to appropriate commodity data streams.

attributes.name: approval_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether changes to this VEE rule require formal approval before activation. True for rules impacting billing or regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: User identifier of the person who approved this VEE rule for production use. Applicable when approval_required_flag is true.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this VEE rule was formally approved for production use. Supports governance and compliance documentation.

attributes.name: audit_trail_enabled_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: VEE Rule Audit Trail Enabled Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether detailed audit logging is enabled for this rule, capturing every application of the rule and its outcomes for compliance and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: billing_quality_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether data passing this VEE rule is considered billing-quality and suitable for revenue calculation. True if the rule ensures billing-grade accuracy.

attributes.name: confidence_threshold_percent
attributes.description: Minimum confidence level (as a percentage) required for estimated values to be accepted as billing-quality. Used in statistical estimation algorithms.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this VEE rule record was first created in the MDM system. Supports audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date after which the VEE rule is no longer active. Nullable for open-ended rules. Supports rule lifecycle management and historical analysis.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which the VEE rule becomes active and is applied to meter data. Supports temporal rule management and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Specific estimation technique used when the rule type is estimation. Defines how missing or invalid interval data is calculated (e.g., linear interpolation, historical average, same-day-last-week). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear_interpolation|historical_average|same_day_last_week|same_day_last_year|regression|zero_fill|prior_value — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: exception_handling_action
attributes.description: Action taken when the rule detects a data quality exception: flag for review, automatically estimate, reject the data, route to manual review, or substitute with a default value.

attributes.name: execution_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which the VEE rule is executed against incoming or historical meter data (real-time, hourly, daily, weekly, on-demand).

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.business_glossary_term: VEE Rule Last Modified By User
attributes.description: User identifier of the person who last modified this VEE rule record. Supports change tracking and accountability.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this VEE rule record was last modified. Supports audit trail and change management.

attributes.name: lookback_period_days
attributes.business_glossary_term: VEE Rule Lookback Period in Days
attributes.description: Number of days of historical data the rule examines for validation or estimation purposes. Used by statistical and pattern-matching algorithms.

attributes.name: lower_limit
attributes.description: Minimum acceptable value for validation rules. Interval data below this limit triggers a validation exception or editing action.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, implementation guidance, or special considerations related to this VEE rule. Supports knowledge transfer and operational documentation.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM Business Practice Standards

attributes.name: owner_group
attributes.description: Business unit or team responsible for maintaining and governing this VEE rule (e.g., Metering Operations, Revenue Assurance, Data Quality Team).

attributes.name: priority_order
attributes.description: Execution sequence priority for the rule within the VEE processing engine. Lower numbers execute first. Determines the order in which multiple rules are applied to the same interval data.

attributes.name: rule_category
attributes.description: Functional category of the rule indicating the specific data quality issue it addresses (e.g., spike detection, zero consumption validation, missing data estimation).

attributes.name: rule_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for the VEE rule, used for external reference and system integration. Typically a short alphanumeric code following utility naming conventions.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM Business Practice Standards

attributes.name: rule_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the VEE rule including its business logic, application context, and expected outcomes when applied to interval meter data.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM Business Practice Standards

attributes.name: rule_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the VEE rule describing its purpose and function within the meter data management process.

attributes.name: rule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the VEE rule indicating whether it is actively applied to meter data processing or in a non-operational state.

attributes.name: rule_type
attributes.description: Classification of the rule within the VEE process: validation (checks data quality), estimation (fills missing data), or editing (corrects erroneous data).

attributes.name: threshold_unit
attributes.business_glossary_term: VEE Rule Threshold Unit of Measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the threshold value (e.g., kWh, MWh, percentage, count, standard deviations) providing context for threshold interpretation.

attributes.name: threshold_value
attributes.description: Numeric threshold parameter used by the rule algorithm to determine data quality exceptions. For example, spike tolerance percentage, maximum consumption limit, or minimum expected value.

attributes.name: upper_limit
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable value for validation rules. Interval data above this limit triggers a validation exception or editing action.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of the VEE rule configuration. Incremented with each modification to support change tracking and rollback capabilities.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User identifier of the person who created this VEE rule record. Supports accountability and audit requirements.

products.name: vee_exception
products.description: Operational record of a VEE processing exception raised during interval data validation or estimation — capturing intervals that failed validation rules and required manual review, automatic re-estimation, or override. Stores exception type, severity, affected interval range (start/end timestamps), VEE rule triggered, auto-resolution status, manual reviewer identifier, resolution action taken (re-estimate/edit/accept/override), resolution timestamp, and exception disposition (resolved/escalated/waived). Supports MDM data quality workflows, operational dashboards for VEE pass rates, and regulatory audit trails for billing data integrity. Key metric: exception rate by rule type drives VEE rule tuning.
products.reference: Oracle Utilities MDM — VEE Exception Management

attributes.name: vee_exception_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the VEE exception record. Primary key for the VEE exception entity.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer account associated with the meter and service point for this VEE exception. Used for customer impact analysis and billing hold workflows.

attributes.name: audit_finding_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit_finding. Business justification: VEE exceptions identified as audit findings when indicating systematic data quality issues or control deficiencies. Supports audit evidence collection, corrective action tracking, regulatory reporting

attributes.name: curtailment_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to renewable.curtailment_event. Business justification: VEE exceptions on DER interval data are frequently caused by curtailment events producing anomalous readings. Linking enables automated VEE resolution by identifying curtailment as root cause — a stan

attributes.name: dr_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to demand.dr_event. Business justification: VEE exceptions during DR event windows require context to determine if anomalous readings are caused by legitimate load curtailment rather than data errors. Linking vee_exception to the active dr_even

attributes.name: event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to outage.outage_event. Business justification: VEE analysts investigate whether missing/anomalous interval readings stem from power interruptions. Regulatory VEE reports require cross-referencing exceptions with outage events to justify estimation

attributes.name: market_settlement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to trading.market_settlement. Business justification: VEE exceptions that correct interval data after initial settlement require settlement restatement. ISO tariffs mandate tracking which market_settlement records are affected by data quality corrections

attributes.name: meter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the meter that generated the interval data which triggered this VEE exception.

attributes.name: meter_point_id
attributes.description: Reference to the service point (delivery location) associated with the meter that generated the interval data for this exception. Used to link exceptions to customer accounts and premises.

attributes.name: primary_vee_interval_reading_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific interval data record that failed VEE validation and raised this exception.

attributes.name: primary_vee_rule_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Rule Identifier
attributes.description: Reference to the VEE rule that was triggered and caused this exception to be raised.

attributes.name: rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the rate schedule (tariff) applicable to the service point at the time of the exception. Used to determine billing impact and priority for resolution, especially for Time-of-Use (TOU) and Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) customers.

attributes.name: to_interval_reading_id
attributes.description: FK to metering.interval_reading.interval_reading_id — VEE exceptions must reference the interval reading(s) that failed validation. Without this link, operators cannot identify and resolve data quality issues.

attributes.name: to_vee_rule_id
attributes.description: FK to metering.vee_rule.vee_rule_id — Each VEE exception must reference the VEE rule that triggered it. This is essential for exception resolution workflows and rule tuning.

attributes.name: auto_resolution_attempted
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the VEE engine attempted automatic resolution of this exception through estimation algorithms. True if auto-resolution was attempted; False if exception was immediately flagged for manual review.

attributes.name: auto_resolution_successful
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether automatic resolution by the VEE engine was successful. True if the engine successfully estimated a replacement value that passed validation; False if auto-resolution failed and manual intervention is required.

attributes.name: billing_impact_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this VEE exception affects customer billing. True if the affected interval data is used in billing determinants and the exception must be resolved before bill calculation; False if the exception is for non-billing data (e.g., operational monitoring, grid analytics).

attributes.name: corrected_value
attributes.description: Final corrected interval data value (in kWh or other unit of measure) after manual review and editing. This is the value that will be used for billing if the exception is resolved. Null if not yet corrected.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this VEE exception record was first created in the MDM system. Audit field for data lineage and record lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: Numeric data quality score (0.00 to 100.00) assigned to the interval data by the VEE engine, indicating confidence in the data accuracy. Lower scores trigger exceptions. Used for trending meter health and VEE rule tuning.

attributes.name: estimated_value
attributes.description: Estimated interval data value (in kWh or other unit of measure) calculated by the VEE engine to replace the invalid or missing original value. Null if estimation was not performed or failed.

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Method used by the VEE engine or analyst to estimate the corrected interval value. Linear interpolation: average of adjacent intervals. Historical average: average of same interval from prior days. Similar day: value from comparable day (same day-of-week, season). Regression: statistical model. Manual entry: analyst-provided value. None: no estimation performed.

attributes.name: exception_disposition
attributes.description: Final disposition category of the VEE exception indicating how it was ultimately handled. Resolved: data corrected and validated. Escalated: sent to engineering or management for further investigation. Waived: accepted without correction per approved business rule or regulatory guidance.

attributes.name: exception_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Number
attributes.description: Business-facing unique exception number assigned to this VEE exception for tracking and audit purposes. Format: VEE-xxxxxxxxxx.

attributes.name: exception_raised_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the VEE exception was first raised by the MDM VEE engine during interval data validation processing. Represents the business event time of exception detection.

attributes.name: exception_severity
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Severity
attributes.description: Severity level of the VEE exception indicating business impact and urgency for resolution. Critical exceptions block billing; high exceptions require immediate review; medium and low exceptions are tracked for quality metrics; informational exceptions are logged for audit only.

attributes.name: exception_source_system
attributes.description: Source system that originated the interval data which triggered this VEE exception. Typically MDM (Meter Data Management) for AMI data, AMI head-end for direct meter reads, SCADA for grid operations data, manual entry for field reads, or billing system for estimated reads.

attributes.name: exception_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the VEE exception. Open: newly raised and awaiting review. In Review: assigned to analyst for investigation. Resolved: corrective action taken and data corrected. Escalated: requires supervisor or engineering review. Waived: exception accepted without correction per business rule. Closed: final disposition recorded and exception archived.

attributes.name: exception_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Type
attributes.description: Classification of the VEE exception indicating the nature of the data quality issue: validation failure (data failed validation rule), estimation failure (unable to estimate missing interval), editing failure (manual edit rejected), missing data (no interval data received), suspect data (data flagged as questionable), or out of range (value exceeds expected bounds).

attributes.name: interval_count
attributes.description: Number of individual interval readings affected by this VEE exception. For 15-minute interval meters, a 1-hour exception would affect 4 intervals.

attributes.name: interval_end_timestamp
attributes.description: End timestamp of the interval data range affected by this VEE exception. Defines the end of the time window containing suspect or invalid data.

attributes.name: interval_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Start timestamp of the interval data range affected by this VEE exception. Defines the beginning of the time window containing suspect or invalid data.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this VEE exception record was last updated. Audit field for tracking changes to exception status, resolution actions, and data corrections.

attributes.name: original_value
attributes.description: Original raw interval data value (in kWh or other unit of measure) that triggered the VEE exception before any estimation or editing was applied.

attributes.name: regulatory_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this VEE exception must be reported to regulatory authorities (e.g., state Public Utility Commission) as part of data quality and billing accuracy compliance reporting. True if reportable; False otherwise.

attributes.name: resolution_action
attributes.description: Action taken to resolve the VEE exception. Re-estimate: apply different estimation algorithm. Manual edit: analyst manually corrected the value. Accept original: original value accepted despite exception. Override: supervisor approved exception without correction. Escalate: sent to engineering for investigation. Waive: exception acknowledged but no correction required per business rule.

attributes.name: resolution_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes entered by the analyst or system documenting the resolution action, rationale for the decision, and any additional context for audit purposes.

attributes.name: resolution_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the VEE exception was resolved (status changed to resolved, waived, or closed). Null if exception is still open or in review. Used to calculate exception aging and VEE team performance metrics.

attributes.name: reviewer_name
attributes.description: Full name of the analyst or system user who reviewed and resolved this VEE exception. Captured for audit trail and operational reporting.

attributes.name: threshold_value
attributes.description: Numeric threshold value defined in the VEE rule that was exceeded or violated, triggering this exception. For example, maximum expected consumption in kWh, or maximum percent deviation from historical average.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the interval data values associated with this exception. Typically kWh (kilowatt-hour) for electric energy consumption, kW for demand, or gas volume units. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: kWh|MWh|kW|kVAR|kVA|CCF|MCF|therms — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: vee_batch_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Batch Identifier
attributes.description: Reference to the VEE processing batch run that raised this exception. Used to group exceptions by processing cycle for operational dashboards and batch-level quality metrics.

products.name: ami_head_end
products.description: Master record for each AMI head-end system instance managing a population of smart meters — the central communication hub for the AMI network. Captures head-end system name, vendor, software version, communication protocol (RF mesh, PLC, cellular), geographic coverage area, maximum device capacity, current enrolled device count, network uptime SLA, integration endpoint details for MDM, and data collection run statistics (scheduled/on-demand collection execution, success rates, timing, and completeness metrics). Supports multi-vendor AMI environments, head-end performance monitoring, and MDM data completeness tracking for VEE processing readiness.

products.name: ami_event
products.description: Operational event and investigation record generated by AMI smart meters and transmitted to the head-end system — covering the full spectrum of AMI-originated events and their investigation lifecycle. Event types include: tamper alerts (with detection method, tamper type such as cover removal/bypass/reverse installation/unauthorized reconnect, investigation status, confirmed theft indicator, estimated unbilled consumption, revenue recovery amount, and law enforcement referral status), power outage notifications (last gasp), power restoration notifications (first breath), communication failures, voltage sag/swell events, reverse energy flow detections, and firmware update events. Stores event type code, event timestamp, meter identifier, event severity, raw event payload, head-end receipt timestamp, downstream notification status, and for tamper/theft events: detection source (AMI alert, field inspection, VEE anomaly), case status, and closure date. SSOT for all AMI-originated events including tamper/theft investigation within the metering domain. Feeds outage management, grid operations, and revenue protection workflows. Supports non-technical loss reporting and PUC-mandated theft-of-service regulatory filings.

products.name: tou_rate_program
products.description: Defines Time-of-Use (TOU) and Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) rate program structures and manages meter point enrollments in those programs. For program definition: specifies program code, peak/off-peak/shoulder period definitions, seasonal schedules, CPP event trigger criteria, applicable customer segments, effective date range, rate period definitions, and regulatory approval reference. For enrollment: tracks meter point association via enrollment records with enrollment ID, enrollment effective date, program end date, enrollment channel (web/CSR/auto), opt-in/opt-out status, and program-specific meter configuration requirements triggered by enrollment. Owned by metering as the SSOT for rate period time definitions that govern interval data classification and enrollment lifecycle; pricing amounts are owned by the billing domain. Enables billing domain to apply correct TOU rate periods to validated interval data and supports demand response domain for CPP event targeting.

attributes.name: last_true_up_date

attributes.description: The rated maximum output capacity of the behind-the-meter generation system in kilowatts (kW). Used to determine interconnection study requirements and export limits.

attributes.name: nem_program_type
attributes.description: The specific NEM tariff program under which the customer is enrolled. NEM 1.0 provides full retail rate credit for exports; NEM 2.0 includes non-bypassable charges; NEM 3.0 uses export compensation rates; VNEM is Virtual Net Energy Metering for multi-tenant properties; NEM-ST is NEM with energy storage.
attributes.references: CPUC Decision 14-03-041, CPUC Decision 16-01-044, CPUC Decision 17-12-022

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special conditions, or operational comments related to the NEM enrollment. May include interconnection study findings, customer requests, or billing exceptions.

attributes.name: permission_to_operate_date

attributes.name: rec_ownership
attributes.description: Identifies who retains ownership of the RECs generated by the system. Customer retains RECs unless contractually assigned to the utility or sold to a third party. Not Applicable if system is not REC-eligible.

attributes.name: storage_capacity_kwh
attributes.description: The rated energy storage capacity of the battery system in kilowatt-hours (kWh). Null if no storage is present. Used to assess demand response and grid services potential.

attributes.name: storage_power_rating_kw
attributes.description: The maximum charge/discharge power rating of the battery system in kilowatts (kW). Null if no storage is present. Determines instantaneous grid support capability.

attributes.name: system_installation_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Distributed Energy Resource (DER) System Installation Date

attributes.name: tariff_reference

attributes.name: termination_date

attributes.name: true_up_period_months
attributes.description: The number of months in the NEM billing cycle before a true-up settlement occurs. Typically 12 months. During the true-up period, excess generation credits are banked; at true-up, remaining credits are settled or forfeited per tariff rules.

attributes.description: Type of remote service action executed via AMI: remote connect, remote disconnect, on-demand meter read, load limiting activation/deactivation, or firmware over-the-air (OTA) update.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Priority level assigned to the remote service order, determining execution sequence in the AMI command queue (critical for safety/emergency, high for revenue protection, normal for routine, low for bulk operations).

attributes.name: reconnect_reason

attributes.name: regulatory_compliance_flag

attributes.name: requested_timestamp

attributes.name: retry_count
attributes.description: Number of times the remote service order has been retried after initial failure, used to track execution persistence and prevent infinite retry loops.

attributes.name: scheduled_execution_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the remote service order is scheduled to be executed on the meter, may differ from requested timestamp for planned actions.

attributes.name: signal_strength_dbm
attributes.description: Signal strength in decibels-milliwatts (dBm) measured at the time of remote service order execution, used to diagnose communication failures.

products.name: invoice
products.description: Core transactional entity representing a utility bill issued to a customer for a billing period, including header-level totals and granular line-item charge detail. At the header level: captures invoice number, billing period dates, due date, total amount due, energy consumed (kWh/MWh), demand (kW), prior balance, current charges, taxes, adjustments, and payment status. At the line level: captures individual charge components including energy charges, demand charges, customer charges, fuel adjustment clauses, distribution riders, taxes, and credits with rate component reference, quantity, unit rate, calculated amount, and applicable billing determinant. Generated from Oracle CC&B and SAP IS-U billing engine. SSOT for all customer-facing billing documents and their charge detail. Supports SOX AR controls, granular revenue recognition, rate component-level analysis, and regulatory rate case evidence.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp

attributes.name: rate_version

attributes.name: revenue_class
attributes.description: Customer class for revenue reporting and regulatory compliance. Aligns with FERC and state PUC revenue classification requirements.

attributes.name: reversal_flag

attributes.name: source_line_reference
attributes.description: Original line item identifier from the source billing system. Maintains traceability to operational system of record for reconciliation and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: source_system_code

products.name: payment
products.description: Transactional record of all customer payment activity including inbound payments received and outbound refunds disbursed against outstanding invoices or account balances. For inbound payments: captures payment date, amount, method (check, ACH, credit card, cash, online, auto-pay), channel (IVR, web, walk-in, mail), reference number, bank routing details, and application status. For outbound refunds: captures refund date, amount, disbursement method (check, ACH, account credit), reason code (overpayment, deposit return, credit balance, billing error), originating credit source, approval status, and disbursement confirmation. Sourced from SAP IS-U FICA and Oracle CC&B payment processing. SSOT for all cash receipts and disbursements in the revenue cycle. Supports cash application controls and SOX compliance.
products.reference: Payment / Cash Receipt

attributes.name: payment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the payment transaction record. Primary key for the payment entity.

attributes.name: account_id

attributes.name: billing_service_agreement_id
attributes.description: FK to billing.service_agreement.service_agreement_id — Payments may be applied at the account/service agreement level when not tied to a specific invoice (e.g., prepayments, deposits).

attributes.name: payment_arrangement_id
attributes.description: Reference to the payment arrangement or installment plan if this payment is part of a structured payment agreement. Null for standard payments.

attributes.name: payment_invoice_id

attributes.name: to_invoice_id
attributes.description: FK to billing.invoice.invoice_id — Payments are applied against specific invoices (or account balances). This FK is critical for cash application and AR reconciliation.

attributes.name: amount
attributes.description: Monetary value of the payment or refund transaction in the billing currency. Positive values for inbound payments, may be positive or negative depending on system convention for refunds.

attributes.name: application_status
attributes.description: Status indicating whether and how the payment has been applied to outstanding invoices or account balance. Tracks cash application workflow completion.

attributes.name: applied_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the payment amount that has been successfully applied to invoices or account balance. May differ from payment_amount if payment is partially applied or includes unapplied credit.
attributes.references: GAAP Revenue Recognition, SAP IS-U FICA

attributes.name: authorization_code
attributes.description: Authorization or approval code returned by the payment processor or card network confirming the transaction was approved. Used for reconciliation and dispute resolution.
attributes.references: PCI DSS, Card Network Operating Regulations

attributes.name: auto_pay_enrollment_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this payment was processed as part of an automatic payment enrollment. True for auto-pay transactions, false for manual payments.

attributes.name: bank_account_number_masked
attributes.description: Masked or tokenized bank account number for ACH payments. Only last 4 digits visible for PCI compliance and fraud prevention. Full account number stored in secure vault.

attributes.name: bank_routing_number
attributes.description: Nine-digit American Bankers Association routing transit number identifying the financial institution for ACH or check payments. Confidential financial data.
attributes.references: NACHA ACH Rules, Federal Reserve ABA Routing Number Directory

attributes.name: batch_reference
attributes.description: Identifier for the payment processing batch if this payment was processed as part of a batch run. Used for lockbox processing, bulk ACH imports, and batch reconciliation.

attributes.name: card_expiration_month
attributes.description: Month component of the payment card expiration date (1-12). Used for recurring payment validation and auto-pay processing.

attributes.name: card_expiration_year
attributes.description: Four-digit year component of the payment card expiration date. Used for recurring payment validation and auto-pay processing.

attributes.name: card_last_four_digits
attributes.description: Last four digits of the payment card number for customer reference and dispute resolution. Full card number never stored per PCI DSS requirements.

attributes.name: card_type
attributes.description: Credit or debit card network brand for card-based payments. Null for non-card payment methods.

attributes.name: currency_code

attributes.name: disbursement_confirmation_number
attributes.description: Confirmation or tracking number for the refund disbursement. May be check number, ACH trace number, or wire transfer confirmation. Null for inbound payments.

attributes.name: disbursement_date
attributes.description: Date when the refund check was issued or electronic refund was transmitted. Null for inbound payments or pending refunds.

attributes.name: gl_account_code

attributes.name: last_modified_by

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this payment record was last updated. Tracks all modifications for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: lockbox_number
attributes.description: Bank lockbox identifier for payments received via lockbox processing service. Null for non-lockbox payments.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments related to the payment transaction. May include customer instructions, dispute details, or special handling notes entered by customer service representatives.

attributes.name: nsf_fee_assessed

attributes.name: payment_date

attributes.name: payment_method
attributes.description: Financial instrument or mechanism used to tender the payment. Identifies whether payment was made via check, electronic funds transfer, card payment, or cash. attributes.references: NACHA ACH Rules, PCI DSS Payment Card Standards

attributes.name: payment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the payment transaction. Tracks progression from initial receipt through clearing and application to customer account balance.

attributes.name: payment_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the payment transaction was recorded in the billing system. Used for audit trail and transaction sequencing.
attributes.references: SOX Internal Controls - IT General Controls

attributes.name: payment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the payment transaction direction and purpose. Inbound payments represent cash receipts from customers; outbound refunds represent disbursements to customers.

attributes.name: posting_date
attributes.description: Accounting date when the payment transaction was posted to the general ledger. May differ from payment_date due to batch processing timing or period-end cutoffs.
attributes.references: GAAP Financial Reporting, SAP S/4HANA FI-GL

attributes.name: reference_number
attributes.description: External reference number or confirmation code for the payment transaction. May include check number, ACH trace number, credit card authorization code, or online payment confirmation ID.

attributes.name: refund_approval_status
attributes.description: Workflow status for refund approval process. Tracks management review and authorization for outbound refund disbursements. Null for inbound payments.

attributes.name: refund_approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the refund was approved for disbursement. Part of the audit trail for financial controls. Null for inbound payments.

attributes.name: refund_approved_by
attributes.description: User ID or name of the employee who authorized the refund disbursement. Required for SOX compliance and audit trail. Null for inbound payments.

attributes.name: refund_method
attributes.description: Method by which the refund is disbursed to the customer. May be check, ACH transfer, account credit, or reversal to original payment method. Null for inbound payments.

attributes.name: refund_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the business reason for issuing a refund to the customer. Null for inbound payments. Used for refund analytics and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: reversal_date
attributes.description: Date when the payment was reversed. Null if payment has not been reversed.

attributes.name: reversal_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this payment transaction has been reversed due to NSF (non-sufficient funds), chargeback, or administrative correction. True if reversed, false otherwise.

attributes.name: reversal_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the reason for payment reversal. Includes NSF returns, chargebacks, disputes, and administrative corrections. Null if payment has not been reversed.
attributes.references: NACHA ACH Return Reason Codes, Card Network Chargeback Reason Codes

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the source system or module that originated the payment transaction record. Examples include SAP IS-U FICA, Oracle CC&B, payment gateway integration, or third-party payment processor.

attributes.name: transaction_reference
attributes.description: Unique transaction identifier assigned by the payment gateway or processor. Used for reconciliation, chargebacks, and technical support inquiries.

attributes.name: unapplied_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the payment amount that remains unapplied and held as account credit. Occurs when payment exceeds outstanding balance or when application is suspended pending dispute resolution.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U FICA Unapplied Cash Management

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier that created this payment record. May be a customer service representative, automated batch process, or payment gateway integration.

products.name: payment_arrangement
products.description: Master entity representing a formal installment or deferred payment plan negotiated with a customer to resolve past-due balances. Captures arrangement type, total amount owed, number of installments, installment amounts, scheduled payment dates, down payment, arrangement status, breach conditions, and associated collections case. Managed within SAP IS-U FICA and Oracle CC&B collections modules.

attributes.description: Unique identifier for the payment arrangement. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U FICA Contract Account Management

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer account for which this payment arrangement was established.

attributes.name: billing_service_agreement_id
attributes.description: FK to billing.service_agreement.service_agreement_id — Payment arrangements are established for a specific service agreement with past-due balances.

attributes.name: counterparty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to trading.counterparty. Business justification: Payment arrangements with wholesale trading counterparties for deferred settlement payments reference the counterparty entity. Required for credit risk management, ISDA/CSA compliance, and counterpart

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the payment arrangement was formally approved and became binding.

attributes.name: arrangement_end_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date when the final installment is due and the arrangement is expected to be completed. Nullable for open-ended arrangements.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U FICA Installment Plan End Date

attributes.name: arrangement_for_collections_case
attributes.description: FK to billing.collections_case.collections_case_id — Payment arrangements are negotiated to resolve a collections case. This FK links the installment plan to the delinquent balance being resolved.

attributes.name: arrangement_number
attributes.description: Business-facing unique identifier for the payment arrangement, typically displayed on customer correspondence and used in collections workflows.

attributes.name: arrangement_start_date

attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the payment arrangement. attributes.name: arrangement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the payment arrangement structure. Installment plan spreads balance over fixed payments; deferred payment postpones full payment to future date; settlement agreement resolves disputed balance; budget billing equalizes monthly payments; hardship plan offers reduced terms for financial distress; promise to pay is short-term commitment.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U FICA Payment Arrangement Category

attributes.name: auto_pay_enrolled_flag

attributes.name: breach_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why the arrangement was breached, typically referencing specific missed payments or violation of terms. Nullable if not breached.

attributes.name: breach_threshold
attributes.description: Maximum number of missed installments allowed before the arrangement is automatically breached and collections actions resume. Typically 1 or 2 missed payments.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B Payment Arrangement Breach Rule

attributes.name: cancellation_date
attributes.description: Date when the payment arrangement was cancelled before completion. Nullable if arrangement was not cancelled.

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why the arrangement was cancelled, such as customer request, account closure, or administrative error. Nullable if not cancelled.

attributes.name: completion_date
attributes.description: Date when all installment obligations were fulfilled and the arrangement was successfully completed. Nullable if not yet completed.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the payment arrangement record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this arrangement. Typically USD for US utilities.

attributes.name: customer_signature_received_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether customer signature or electronic acceptance was obtained for the arrangement terms, required for enforceability.

attributes.name: down_payment_amount
attributes.description: Initial payment required at arrangement establishment to demonstrate good faith and reduce the principal balance before installments begin. Zero if no down payment required.

attributes.name: down_payment_received_date
attributes.description: Date when the down payment was actually received and posted to the account. Nullable if down payment not yet received or not required.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U FICA Payment Document Date

attributes.name: first_installment_due_date
attributes.description: Date when the first scheduled installment payment is due, typically 30 days after arrangement start date or aligned with customer billing cycle.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U FICA First Due Date

attributes.name: installment_amount
attributes.description: Fixed amount due for each regular installment payment. Calculated by dividing remaining balance after down payment by number of installments.

attributes.name: installment_frequency
attributes.description: Cadence at which installment payments are scheduled. Monthly is most common for utility payment arrangements.

attributes.name: installments_missed_count
attributes.description: Number of scheduled installment payments that were not received by their due date. Exceeding the allowed threshold triggers breach status.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U FICA Missed Payment Count

attributes.name: installments_paid_count
attributes.description: Number of installment payments successfully received and posted to date. Used to track customer compliance with arrangement terms.

Bridges metering domain MDM output to the billing engine for rate calculation. Critical for TOU, CPP, and demand-based rate schedules.

attributes.name: billing_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days in the billing period. Used for pro-ration calculations, average daily usage metrics, and normalization of consumption data for year-over-year comparisons.

attributes.name: billing_multiplier
attributes.description: Multiplier applied to meter readings to account for Current Transformer (CT) and Potential Transformer (PT) ratios in high-voltage metering installations. Converts secondary meter readings to primary consumption values. Typically greater than 1 for commercial and industrial customers.

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: Method used to derive the billing determinants from meter data. Indicates whether values were calculated from actual interval data, estimated due to missing data, or derived using special algorithms for net metering or demand windowing.

attributes.name: calculation_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the billing determinants were calculated from validated meter interval data. Represents the business event time when MDM output was transformed into billing inputs.

attributes.name: comments

attributes.name: contract_demand_kw
attributes.description: The contracted maximum demand level agreed upon between the utility and customer. Used for rate schedules where customers commit to a minimum demand level in exchange for favorable pricing. Excess demand above this level may incur penalty charges.
attributes.references: FERC Rate Design; PUC Commercial Rate Schedules

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this billing determinant record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Internal Controls; SAP IS-U Audit

attributes.name: critical_peak_kwh
attributes.description: Energy consumption during Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) event hours. Used for CPP rate schedules where utilities invoke premium pricing during grid stress events (typically 10-15 days per year).
attributes.references: FERC CPP Rate Design; PUC Demand Response Programs

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: Composite score (0-100) representing the quality of the underlying meter interval data used to calculate these determinants. Considers factors such as percentage of actual vs estimated readings, validation rule pass rate, and data completeness. Used to flag determinants requiring manual review.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM VEE; SAP IS-U Device Management

attributes.name: estimated_interval_count
attributes.description: Number of meter intervals that were estimated rather than actual readings. Used for data quality assessment and to flag billing determinants that may require review due to missing or invalid meter data.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM VEE; ANSI C12.19

attributes.name: interval_count
attributes.description: Number of meter interval readings used to calculate these billing determinants. Typically 2,880 intervals for 15-minute data over a 30-day period, or 1,440 intervals for 30-minute data. Used for data quality validation.

attributes.name: is_final_determinant
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this is the final, validated billing determinant record for the billing period (true) or a preliminary/estimated version (false). Used to prevent duplicate billing and ensure only validated determinants are passed to the billing engine.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B Billing; SAP IS-U Billing

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this billing determinant record was last updated. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and identifying records that have been manually adjusted after initial calculation.
attributes.references: SOX Internal Controls; SAP IS-U Audit

attributes.name: load_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of average load to peak load during the billing period, calculated as (total_kwh / (peak_demand_kw * billing_hours)). Indicates how efficiently the customer uses their peak capacity. Values range from 0 to 1, with higher values indicating more consistent usage patterns.

attributes.name: mid_peak_kwh
attributes.description: Energy consumption during mid-peak TOU periods (shoulder hours between on-peak and off-peak). Used for TOU rate schedules with three-tier time-based pricing.
attributes.references: FERC TOU Rate Design; PUC Rate Schedule

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier of the person or process that last modified this billing determinant record. Used for audit trail and accountability in SOX compliance reporting.

attributes.name: net_metering_export_kwh

attributes.references: PURPA; State NEM Regulations; FERC Order 2222

attributes.name: net_metering_import_kwh
attributes.description: Energy imported from the grid by customers with Distributed Energy Resources (DER). Used for Net Energy Metering (NEM) rate schedules to calculate net consumption after accounting for on-site generation.
attributes.references: PURPA; State NEM Regulations; FERC Order 2222

attributes.name: off_peak_demand_kw
attributes.description: Maximum power demand during off-peak TOU periods. Used for rate schedules that apply separate demand charges for off-peak periods.
attributes.references: FERC TOU Rate Design; PUC Rate Schedule

attributes.name: off_peak_kwh
attributes.description: Energy consumption during off-peak TOU periods (typically nights and weekends when grid demand is lower). Used for TOU rate calculations with discounted pricing.
attributes.references: FERC TOU Rate Design; PUC Rate Schedule

attributes.name: on_peak_demand_kw
attributes.description: Maximum power demand during on-peak TOU periods. Used for rate schedules that apply separate demand charges for on-peak versus off-peak periods.
attributes.references: FERC TOU Rate Design; PUC Rate Schedule

attributes.name: on_peak_kwh
attributes.description: Energy consumption during on-peak TOU periods (typically weekday afternoons when grid demand is highest). Used for TOU and CPP rate calculations with premium pricing.
attributes.references: FERC TOU Rate Design; PUC Rate Schedule

attributes.name: peak_demand_kw
attributes.description: Maximum instantaneous power demand in kilowatts recorded during the billing period. Used for demand-based rate schedules common in commercial and industrial tariffs. Typically measured as the highest 15-minute or 30-minute interval average.

attributes.name: peak_demand_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the peak demand (kW) occurred during the billing period. Used for demand response analysis, load profiling, and customer engagement regarding demand management opportunities.

attributes.name: power_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of real power (kW) to apparent power (kVA) during the billing period, typically calculated at the time of peak demand. Used to assess power quality and apply power factor adjustment charges. Values range from 0 to 1, with 1.0 representing ideal unity power factor.

attributes.name: ratchet_demand_kw
attributes.description: Demand value used for ratchet clause billing, typically a percentage (e.g., 80%) of the highest demand recorded in the previous 11 months. Used in commercial and industrial rate schedules to ensure minimum demand charges even during low-usage months.
attributes.references: FERC Rate Design; PUC Commercial Rate Schedules

attributes.name: reactive_demand_kvar
attributes.description: Maximum reactive power demand in kilovolt-amperes reactive during the billing period. Used for power factor penalties or reactive power charges in industrial and large commercial rate schedules.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: System of record from which the meter interval data originated. Indicates whether data came from Meter Data Management (MDM), Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI), manual meter reading, estimation algorithms, or SCADA systems.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDM; SAP IS-U Device Management

attributes.name: temperature_normalized_kwh
attributes.description: Energy consumption adjusted for weather variations using heating degree days (HDD) and cooling degree days (CDD). Used for load forecasting, energy efficiency program evaluation, and customer usage comparisons across different weather conditions.

attributes.name: total_kwh
attributes.description: Total energy consumption in kilowatt-hours for the billing period. Sum of all interval data across all Time-of-Use (TOU) periods. Primary determinant for energy charges.

attributes.name: tou_period_1_kwh
attributes.description: Energy consumption for TOU period 1 as defined in the rate schedule. Supports rate schedules with custom TOU period definitions beyond standard on-peak/off-peak/mid-peak classifications.
attributes.references: FERC TOU Rate Design; PUC Rate Schedule

attributes.name: tou_period_2_kwh
attributes.description: Energy consumption for TOU period 2 as defined in the rate schedule. Supports rate schedules with custom TOU period definitions beyond standard on-peak/off-peak/mid-peak classifications.
attributes.references: FERC TOU Rate Design; PUC Rate Schedule

attributes.name: tou_period_3_kwh
attributes.description: Energy consumption for TOU period 3 as defined in the rate schedule. Supports rate schedules with custom TOU period definitions beyond standard on-peak/off-peak/mid-peak classifications.
attributes.references: FERC TOU Rate Design; PUC Rate Schedule

attributes.name: tou_period_4_kwh

attributes.references: FERC TOU Rate Design; PUC Rate Schedule

products.name: adjustment
products.description: Transactional record of a financial adjustment applied to a customer account or invoice, including credits, debits, rebates, rate corrections, estimated-to-actual true-ups, regulatory surcharge adjustments, and NEM (Net Energy Metering) credits for behind-the-meter generation. Captures adjustment type, reason code, amount, affected billing period, approval status, authorizing user, and source invoice reference. For NEM credit adjustments: stores exported kWh, credit rate ($/kWh), credit amount, cumulative credit balance, credit expiration date, and applicable NEM tariff version. Sourced from SAP IS-U FICA, Oracle CC&B adjustment processing, and NEM billing modules. SSOT for all financial adjustments including NEM credits. Supports SOX financial controls, revenue recognition, and state NEM/RPS regulatory compliance reporting.

attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code indicating the currency in which the adjustment amount is denominated.

attributes.name: dispute_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this adjustment is related to a customer dispute or complaint resolution. True if dispute-related, False otherwise.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B Dispute Management; SAP IS-U Complaint Handling

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which the adjustment becomes effective for accounting and revenue recognition purposes. May differ from adjustment_date for backdated corrections.
