attributes.description: Externally visible alphanumeric reference number assigned to this trouble call at receipt, used for customer-facing acknowledgement (e.g., IVR confirmation code, agent ticket number, web portal confirmation). Sourced from the CIS or OMS call intake module.
attributes.references: SAP IS-U; Oracle Utilities CC&B — Call Management

attributes.name: reported_symptom_code
attributes.description: Standardized code representing the symptom or problem reported by the caller or detected by the AMI system (e.g., FULL_OUTAGE, PARTIAL_OUTAGE, FLICKERING, LOW_VOLTAGE, DOWNED_LINE, BURNING_SMELL). Sourced from the OMS symptom code reference table. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FULL_OUTAGE|PARTIAL_OUTAGE|FLICKERING|LOW_VOLTAGE|DOWNED_LINE|BURNING_SMELL|SPARKING|BUZZING — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: GE PowerOn ADMS — OMS Symptom Codes; IEEE 1366

attributes.name: reported_symptom_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of the outage symptom or problem as reported by the caller or transcribed by the call center agent. Supplements the structured symptom code with verbatim customer language for OMS analysis and crew dispatch context.

products.name: obligation

products.name: audit_finding
products.description: Individual compliance deficiency, exception, gap, or near-miss record identified through formal audit, internal monitoring, control testing, self-assessment, or operational review. Covers NERC CIP potential violations (PVs), FERC market rule violations, PUC service quality deficiencies, SOX control deficiencies, internally discovered compliance exceptions, and proactive near-miss identifications. Captures finding reference number, associated audit (if audit-originated), violated standard or rule citation, severity classification, discovery method (external audit, internal audit, self-monitoring, employee report, control testing), finding description, root cause category, risk severity, business unit responsible, remediation due date, and escalation status (including whether self-reporting is warranted). Serves as the single register for all compliance deficiencies regardless of discovery channel — from formal audit findings to internally identified exceptions. Drives the enforcement and corrective action workflow, and feeds the self-report filing process when internal findings warrant proactive disclosure.
products.reference: NERC Violation Risk Factor / Violation Severity Level Matrix; FERC Enforcement Advisory

products.name: enforcement_action
products.description: Record of formal enforcement actions, associated monetary penalties, and sanctions initiated by regulators against the utility, including NERC Notice of Alleged Violation (NAV) with civil monetary penalties (CMPs), FERC Order to Show Cause with civil penalties, PUC complaint proceedings with fines, EPA Notice of Violation (NOV) with administrative penalties, and OSHA citations. Captures action type, issuing agency, docket or case number, alleged violation description, proposed penalty amount, final penalty assessed, payment due date, payment status, penalty mitigation factors applied (compliance history, self-reporting credit, cooperation), contested flag, settlement terms, action resolution date, and financial exposure classification. Serves as SSOT for all regulatory enforcement posture, penalty assessment and tracking, financial exposure reporting to the Board and external auditors, and penalty payment reconciliation.
products.reference: NERC Enforcement; FERC Enforcement; EPA Civil Enforcement

attributes.description: Indicates whether the asset has connectivity to networks outside the ESP, requiring additional CIP-005 controls.

attributes.name: firmware_version
attributes.description: Current firmware or software version installed on the asset. Critical for CIP-007 patch management and vulnerability tracking.

attributes.name: in_service_date
attributes.description: Date the asset was placed into operational service. Used to determine when CIP compliance obligations begin.

attributes.name: ip_address
attributes.description: IP address assigned to the cyber asset. Required for Electronic Access Point (EAP) and ESP boundary documentation under CIP-005.

attributes.name: last_cip_assessment_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Last CIP (Critical Infrastructure Protection) Assessment Date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent CIP impact assessment or classification review for this asset, as required under CIP-002.

attributes.name: last_patch_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent security patch or software update applied to this asset. Required for CIP-007 patch management compliance.

attributes.name: last_vulnerability_assessment_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent vulnerability assessment performed on this asset, as required under CIP-007 and CIP-010.

attributes.name: mac_address
attributes.description: MAC address of the network interface. Used for device identification and access control under CIP-005 and CIP-007.

attributes.name: manufacturer
attributes.description: Manufacturer or vendor of the asset hardware or software (e.g., GE, Siemens, ABB, Cisco, OSIsoft).

attributes.name: model_number
attributes.description: Model or part number of the asset. Used for vulnerability assessment and patch management under CIP-007.

attributes.name: network_zone
attributes.description: Logical network zone or segment where the asset resides (e.g., Control Network, Corporate Network, DMZ). Used for ESP boundary definition.

attributes.name: next_cip_assessment_due_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Next CIP (Critical Infrastructure Protection) Assessment Due Date
attributes.description: Date by which the next CIP impact assessment or classification review must be completed. CIP-002 requires reassessment within 15 calendar months of the previous assessment.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or context regarding the CIP classification, assessment, or compliance status of this asset.

attributes.name: removable_media_controls_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this asset requires CIP-011 removable media controls (USB drives, CDs, external hard drives).

attributes.name: routable_protocol_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether the asset uses routable protocols (TCP/IP) that require Electronic Access Point (EAP) controls under CIP-005.

attributes.name: transient_cyber_asset
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is a transient cyber asset (e.g., laptop, tablet, removable media) used for diagnostic testing, maintenance, or troubleshooting, subject to CIP-010 transient device controls.

attributes.name: updated_by
attributes.description: User ID or name of the person who last updated this CIP asset record. Required for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this CIP asset record was last modified. Required for audit trail and change tracking under CIP-010.

Supports EPA Clean Air Act Title IV Acid Rain Program, CSAPR, and state RPS compliance.

attributes.name: power_plant_id

attributes.name: primary_emissions_obligation_id

attributes.name: allowances_held
attributes.description: The number of emission allowances held by the facility for the pollutant type at the end of the reporting period, applicable to cap-and-trade programs.

attributes.name: allowances_used
attributes.description: The number of emission allowances used (surrendered) to cover emissions during the reporting period, applicable to cap-and-trade programs.

attributes.name: amendment_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this report is an amendment to a previously submitted report (True) or an original submission (False).

attributes.name: amendment_reason

attributes.name: applicable_emission_limit
attributes.description: The regulatory emission limit applicable to this facility and pollutant type for the reporting period, expressed in the same unit as measured emissions.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act, CSAPR, State RPS

attributes.name: authorized_representative_name
attributes.description: The name of the designated authorized representative who certifies the accuracy of the emissions report on behalf of the facility.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: cems_certification_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS) Certification Status
attributes.description: The certification status of the CEMS equipment used for emissions monitoring, if applicable.

attributes.name: certification_date
attributes.description: The date when the authorized representative certified the emissions report as accurate and complete.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Additional comments, notes, or explanatory information related to the emissions report.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: compliance_margin
attributes.description: The difference between the applicable emission limit and the measured emission quantity. Positive values indicate compliance; negative values indicate exceedance.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: The overall compliance status of the facility for this emissions report: Compliant (within limits), Non-Compliant (exceeded limits), Pending Review, or Conditional (compliant with conditions).
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV, CSAPR

attributes.name: corrective_action_plan
attributes.description: Description of the corrective action plan implemented or planned to address non-compliance, if applicable.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this emissions report record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: data_quality_indicator
attributes.description: Indicator of the quality and completeness of the emissions data: Verified (QA/QC complete), Estimated (based on calculations), Provisional (preliminary data), or Incomplete (missing data elements).

attributes.name: emission_rate
attributes.description: The calculated emission rate for the pollutant, typically expressed as pounds per MMBtu or tons per MWh, depending on the regulatory program.

attributes.name: emission_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit of measure for the reported emission quantity (typically tons, but may include pounds or kilograms for certain pollutants).
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: exceedance_reason
attributes.description: Explanation or reason code for any emission limit exceedance, if applicable. Null if no exceedance occurred.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: gross_generation_mwh
attributes.description: The total gross electrical generation from the plant unit during the reporting period, measured in megawatt-hours (MWh).
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: heat_input_mmbtu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Heat Input Million British Thermal Units (MMBtu)
attributes.description: The total heat input to the generation unit during the reporting period, measured in million British thermal units (MMBtu).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this emissions report record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: measured_emission_quantity
attributes.description: The measured quantity of emissions for the specified pollutant during the reporting period, expressed in tons.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV, 40 CFR Part 75

attributes.name: monitoring_methodology
attributes.description: The methodology used to measure emissions: CEMS (Continuous Emissions Monitoring System), PEMS (Predictive Emissions Monitoring System), Alternative monitoring, Fuel Sampling, or Mass Balance calculation.

attributes.name: operating_hours
attributes.description: The total number of operating hours for the plant unit during the reporting period.

attributes.name: orispl_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Office of Regulatory Information Systems Plant Location (ORISPL) Code
attributes.description: The unique EPA-assigned ORISPL code identifying the power plant facility for regulatory reporting purposes.

attributes.name: pollutant_type
attributes.description: The type of pollutant being reported: SO2 (Sulfur Dioxide), NOx (Nitrogen Oxides), CO2 (Carbon Dioxide), Mercury, PM2.5 (Particulate Matter 2.5 micrometers), or PM10 (Particulate Matter 10 micrometers).

attributes.name: qa_qc_completion_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Quality Assurance Quality Control (QA/QC) Completion Date
attributes.description: The date when quality assurance and quality control procedures were completed for the emissions data.

attributes.name: report_submission_date
attributes.description: The date when the emissions report was submitted to the regulatory agency (EPA or state environmental agency).
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: reporting_period_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the emissions reporting period covered by this report.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: reporting_period_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the emissions reporting period covered by this report.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: submission_status
attributes.description: The current status of the emissions report submission to the regulatory agency.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV

products.name: environmental_permit
products.description: Master record for all environmental operating permits held by the utility, including EPA Title V air permits, NPDES water discharge permits, RCRA hazardous waste permits, and state-issued environmental authorizations. Captures permit number, issuing agency, permitted facility, permit type, issuance date, expiration date, renewal status, permitted emission or discharge limits, and permit conditions. SSOT for environmental permit portfolio management.
products.reference: EPA Title V Operating Permit; NPDES Permit; RCRA Permit

attributes.name: environmental_permit_id
attributes.description: Primary key for environmental_permit

attributes.name: power_plant_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the generation, transmission, or distribution facility covered by this environmental permit. Links permit to the physical asset location where environmental compliance is enforced.

attributes.name: primary_environmental_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: Each environmental permit fulfills a specific regulatory obligation (e.g., EPA Title V air permit, NPDES water discharge permit). Many permits can fulfill one obligation (1:N). Adding obligation_id FK

attributes.name: appeal_status
attributes.description: Status of any administrative or judicial appeal of permit conditions. Appeals can delay permit effectiveness or result in modified conditions.
attributes.references: EPA Administrative Appeals Process, Environmental Appeals Board

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this permit record was first created in the compliance management system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system from which this permit record was ingested (e.g., SAP EHS, environmental compliance database, regulatory agency portal). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date the environmental permit becomes legally binding and enforceable. May differ from issuance date if permit includes a delayed effective date provision.

attributes.name: enforcement_action_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this permit is currently subject to an active enforcement action, consent decree, or compliance order from the regulatory agency.
attributes.references: EPA Enforcement and Compliance History Online (ECHO)

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date the environmental permit expires and must be renewed. Operating beyond expiration without renewal constitutes a violation subject to enforcement action and penalties.
attributes.references: EPA Permit Renewal Requirements, Clean Air Act Section 502(b)(5)

attributes.name: facility_epa_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Facility EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) Identification Number
attributes.description: The unique EPA facility identification number assigned to the permitted facility. Used for all federal environmental reporting including emissions inventories and discharge monitoring reports.

attributes.name: facility_name
attributes.description: Name of the utility facility covered by this environmental permit. Typically a power generation plant, substation, or operations center subject to environmental regulation.

attributes.name: issuance_date
attributes.description: The date the environmental permit was officially issued by the regulatory agency. Marks the beginning of the permit term and the effective date for permit conditions.

attributes.name: issuing_agency
attributes.description: Name of the federal, state, or local regulatory agency that issued the environmental permit. Typically EPA for federal permits or state environmental protection agency for state-delegated programs.
attributes.references: EPA Regional Offices, State Environmental Protection Agencies

attributes.name: issuing_agency_jurisdiction
attributes.description: The governmental jurisdiction level of the issuing agency. Determines the regulatory authority hierarchy and appeal process for permit conditions.
attributes.references: EPA Jurisdictional Framework, State Environmental Law

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent regulatory agency inspection of the permitted facility for compliance with permit conditions. Inspections may be routine or triggered by complaints or violations.

attributes.name: last_inspection_result
attributes.description: Outcome of the most recent regulatory inspection. Major violations may result in enforcement actions, penalties, or permit modifications.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this permit record was last modified. Tracks changes to permit status, conditions, or administrative data for compliance audit purposes.

attributes.name: monitoring_frequency
attributes.description: Required frequency for monitoring and reporting emissions or discharges under this permit. Determines compliance testing schedule and data submission deadlines to regulatory agencies.
attributes.references: EPA Continuous Emission Monitoring (CEM) Requirements, 40 CFR Part 60

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special circumstances, or historical context related to this permit. Used for internal compliance management and knowledge transfer.

attributes.name: permit_conditions_summary
attributes.description: High-level summary of key permit conditions, operational restrictions, and compliance obligations. Detailed conditions are maintained in permit documentation repository.

attributes.name: permit_document_url
attributes.description: URL or file path to the official permit document in the document management system. Provides access to full permit text, conditions, and attachments.

attributes.name: permit_fee_amount
attributes.description: Annual or one-time fee paid to the regulatory agency for permit issuance, renewal, or maintenance. Fee structure varies by permit type and jurisdiction.
attributes.references: EPA Permit Fee Schedule, State Environmental Fee Regulations

attributes.name: permit_fee_currency
attributes.description: Currency code for permit fees. Typically USD for US-based utility operations.

attributes.name: permit_number
attributes.description: The official permit number issued by the regulatory agency. This is the externally-known unique identifier used in all regulatory correspondence and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: EPA Title V Operating Permit Program, NPDES Permit Program

attributes.name: permit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the environmental permit. Active permits authorize operations; expired or suspended permits require immediate remediation to avoid enforcement action.
attributes.references: EPA Permit Compliance Framework, State Environmental Agency Standards

attributes.name: permit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the environmental permit based on the regulatory program and environmental media regulated. Determines applicable compliance requirements and reporting obligations.
attributes.references: EPA Environmental Permit Classification, Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, RCRA

attributes.name: permitted_discharge_limit_gallons_per_day
attributes.description: Maximum allowable daily water discharge volume in gallons per day under NPDES or state water discharge permit. Applies to cooling water, process water, and stormwater discharges.
attributes.references: NPDES Permit Program, Clean Water Act Section 402

attributes.name: permitted_emission_limit_tons_per_year
attributes.description: Maximum allowable annual emissions in tons per year for regulated air pollutants under this permit. Exceeding this limit constitutes a permit violation and triggers enforcement action.
attributes.references: EPA Title V Operating Permit, Clean Air Act Section 112

attributes.name: public_comment_period_end_date
attributes.description: Date the public comment period closed for this permit. After this date, the permit becomes final unless appealed.

attributes.name: public_notice_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this permit was subject to public notice and comment period as required for major permits under EPA regulations. Public participation is required for Title V and major NPDES permits.
attributes.references: EPA Public Participation Requirements, 40 CFR Part 124

attributes.name: regulated_pollutants
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of specific pollutants regulated under this permit (e.g., SO2, NOx, PM2.5, mercury, lead, benzene). Each pollutant may have individual emission or discharge limits and monitoring requirements.
attributes.references: EPA National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS), Clean Water Act Effluent Guidelines

attributes.name: renewal_application_date
attributes.description: The date the permit renewal application was submitted to the regulatory agency. Must typically be submitted 6-18 months before expiration depending on permit type and jurisdiction.
attributes.references: EPA Permit Renewal Timelines, 40 CFR Part 70

attributes.name: renewal_status
attributes.description: Current status of the permit renewal process. Tracks whether renewal application has been submitted and the agencys decision status. Critical for avoiding permit lapses.
attributes.references: EPA Permit Renewal Process, State Permit Program Requirements

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: Required frequency for submitting compliance reports to the regulatory agency. Missed reporting deadlines can result in notices of violation and penalties.
attributes.references: EPA Compliance Reporting Requirements, State Environmental Reporting Standards

attributes.name: responsible_party_email
attributes.description: Email address of the responsible official for regulatory correspondence and compliance notifications related to this permit.

attributes.name: responsible_party_name
attributes.description: Name of the individual or role designated as the responsible official for this permit as reported to the regulatory agency. This person certifies compliance reports and permit applications.

attributes.name: responsible_party_phone
attributes.description: Phone number of the responsible official for urgent regulatory communications and compliance inquiries.

attributes.name: responsible_party_title
attributes.description: Job title of the responsible official for this permit. Typically a senior operations or environmental manager with authority to certify compliance.

attributes.name: special_conditions_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this permit includes special or non-standard conditions beyond typical permit requirements. Special conditions often require enhanced monitoring or operational controls.

attributes.name: violation_count
attributes.description: Total number of documented violations of this permit since issuance. High violation counts may trigger enhanced oversight or permit revocation proceedings.

attributes.name: compliance_rec_certificate_id

attributes.description: Identifier of the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) or REC purchase contract under which this REC was acquired. Links to contract management system for terms and conditions.

attributes.name: primary_compliance_power_plant_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the renewable energy generation facility that produced the energy for which this REC was issued. Links to the generation asset registry.

The regulatory_filing table has rps_compliance_year, rps_rec_retired_count, rps_renewable_en

attributes.name: certificate_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the REC certificate. Active certificates are available for trading or retirement; retired certificates have been used for compliance; transferred certificates have changed ownership; cancelled certificates are voided.

attributes.name: compliance_credit_mwh
attributes.description: Effective compliance credit value after applying any multipliers. Calculated as energy_quantity_mwh × rec_multiplier. This is the value counted toward RPS obligation fulfillment.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this REC certificate record was first created in the internal compliance tracking system. Used for audit trail and data lineage purposes.

attributes.name: current_owner_name
attributes.description: Name of the current legal owner of this REC certificate. Ownership may transfer multiple times before retirement. Confidential business information.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system or registry from which this REC data was ingested (e.g., WREGIS API, M-RETS feed, manual entry). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: eligibility_flags
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of special eligibility attributes or certifications for this REC (e.g., in-state, new facility, low-impact hydro, community solar). Used to match RECs to specific compliance requirements.

attributes.name: emissions_avoided_co2_tons
attributes.description: Estimated tons of CO2 emissions avoided by the renewable generation represented by this REC, calculated using regional grid emission factors. Used for environmental impact reporting.

attributes.name: energy_quantity_mwh
attributes.description: Quantity of renewable energy represented by this REC certificate, measured in megawatt-hours. Typically one REC equals one MWh of renewable generation, though some programs use different ratios.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date after which this REC can no longer be used for compliance purposes in the applicable jurisdiction. Many RPS programs impose vintage limits (e.g., RECs must be used within 3 years of generation).

attributes.name: facility_location_country
attributes.description: Country where the generating facility is located. Most U.S. state RPS programs only accept RECs from facilities in the U.S. or specific Canadian provinces.

attributes.name: facility_location_state
attributes.description: U.S. state or Canadian province where the generating facility is located. Geographic location affects RPS eligibility in many jurisdictions.
attributes.references: EIA-860, State RPS Geographic Eligibility Rules

attributes.name: generation_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the generation period for which this REC was issued. Defines the end of the time window during which the renewable energy was produced.

attributes.name: generation_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the generation period for which this REC was issued. Defines the beginning of the time window during which the renewable energy was produced.

attributes.name: generation_technology_type
attributes.description: Type of renewable energy technology used to generate the electricity represented by this REC. Critical for RPS compliance as many states have technology-specific requirements or multipliers. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: solar|wind|hydro|biomass|geothermal|landfill gas|tidal|wave — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: generation_vintage_month
attributes.description: Calendar month (1-12) in which the renewable energy was generated. Provides granular vintage tracking for compliance and trading purposes.

attributes.name: generation_vintage_year
attributes.description: Calendar year in which the renewable energy was generated. Vintage year determines eligibility for compliance periods under state RPS programs.

attributes.name: issuance_date
attributes.description: Date on which this REC certificate was issued by the registry. Issuance typically occurs after generation data is verified and submitted to the registry.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this REC certificate record was last updated in the internal compliance tracking system. Tracks data currency and change history.

attributes.name: last_transfer_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent ownership transfer of this REC. Null if the REC has never been transferred from the original owner.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments regarding this REC certificate, including special handling instructions, compliance considerations, or audit findings. Used for operational coordination and compliance documentation.

attributes.name: original_owner_name
attributes.description: Name of the original owner to whom this REC was first issued, typically the generator or the entity with contractual rights to the RECs from the generation facility.

attributes.name: purchase_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the purchase price. Typically USD for U.S. REC markets.

attributes.name: purchase_price_per_rec
attributes.description: Price paid per REC certificate in the most recent transaction, typically in USD. Confidential commercial information used for cost tracking and portfolio valuation.

attributes.name: rec_multiplier
attributes.description: Multiplier applied to the energy quantity for compliance credit calculation. Some state RPS programs provide enhanced credit (e.g., 1.5x or 2.0x) for certain technologies, in-state generation, or other policy objectives.

attributes.name: rec_serial_number
attributes.description: Unique serial number assigned by the registry to this REC certificate. This is the externally-known business identifier used for tracking, trading, and retirement of the certificate across registries and market participants.
attributes.references: WREGIS, NEPOOL GIS, PJM GATS, M-RETS Registry Standards

attributes.name: registry_name
attributes.description: Name of the registry system where this REC is registered and tracked. Registries provide independent verification and tracking of renewable energy generation and certificate lifecycle. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WREGIS|NEPOOL GIS|PJM GATS|M-RETS|NAR|ERCOT|MIRECS — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date on which this REC was retired for compliance or voluntary purposes. Retired RECs cannot be traded or reused. Null if the REC has not been retired.

attributes.name: retirement_reason
attributes.description: Reason for retiring this REC certificate. RPS compliance retirements are used to meet state renewable portfolio standards; voluntary retirements support corporate sustainability goals or green marketing claims.

attributes.name: rps_compliance_year
attributes.description: Compliance year for which this REC was retired to meet RPS obligations. Null if not retired for RPS compliance. Critical for demonstrating compliance to state PUCs.

attributes.name: rps_tier
attributes.description: RPS tier or category classification for this REC under the applicable state program. Many states have tiered structures with different technology eligibility and compliance requirements for each tier.

attributes.name: transfer_count
attributes.description: Number of times this REC has been transferred between owners since issuance. Provides insight into market activity and trading liquidity.

attributes.name: administrative_law_judge

attributes.name: approved_rate_increase_percent

attributes.name: case_description

attributes.name: case_status

attributes.name: commission_staff_analyst

domains.description: Customer and third-party interconnection requests for distributed generation, solar installations, battery storage, EV chargers, and other BTM resources. Manages interconnection applications, technical reviews, impact studies, POI specifications, NEM agreements, queue management, and SGIP compliance for DER integration. Distinct from renewable (resource management) — focuses on the application and approval process for grid connection.

products.name: application
products.description: Master record for a customer or third-party application to interconnect a distributed energy resource (DER) — solar PV, battery storage, EV charger, CHP, wind, or other BTM resource — to the utility distribution grid. Captures applicant identity, DER technology type, proposed capacity (kW/kVA), point of interconnection (POI), service address, application tier (Level 1/2/3 or Fast Track per applicable interconnection rules), applicable regulatory framework (CPUC Rule 21, FERC Order 2023, state-specific), application date, current queue position, assigned review engineer, and overall application lifecycle status. Also manages the complete application document package — including document type (single-line diagram, site plan, equipment specification sheet, inverter datasheet, UL 1741 certification, load calculation, executed agreement, insurance certificate, permit, as-built drawing), document name, file reference, submission date, submitted by (applicant or utility), document status (received, under review, accepted, rejected, superseded), rejection reason, required resubmission deadline, and completeness determination outcome. This is the SSOT for all interconnection requests and the anchor entity for the entire interconnection domain, including full document lifecycle management for application completeness determination.

products.name: impact_study
products.description: Record of a formal grid impact study ordered for an interconnection application that fails Fast Track or simplified review screens. Captures study type (Feasibility Study, System Impact Study, Facilities Study per FERC Order 2023 or state PUC rules), study scope (affected network segments, contingency scenarios), study contractor (utility internal or third-party), study initiation and completion dates, study cost estimate, cost responsibility allocation reference, identified network upgrades required, upgrade cost estimate, and study findings summary. Also manages cluster/group study cohorts formed under FERC Order 2023 — including cluster study group identifier, geographic study area (feeder, substation zone, planning area), study group formation date, number of applications in group, group study cost allocation methodology, study type classification (cluster feasibility, cluster system impact, cluster facilities), and group study contractor assignment. Supports both individual application studies and FERC Order 2023 cluster study processing for efficient handling of high-volume DER interconnection queues. Drives the determination of required network upgrades and cost allocation across grouped applications.

attributes.name: permit_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether regulatory or municipal permits are required to execute this network upgrade. True if permitting is needed, false otherwise.

attributes.name: permit_status
attributes.description: Current status of permit applications required for the network upgrade. Tracks regulatory approval progress for projects requiring external authorization.

attributes.name: poi_location
attributes.description: Geographic or network location description of the point where the DER will interconnect to the utility grid. Defines the specific connection point driving the upgrade need.

attributes.name: queue_position
attributes.description: Position of the associated interconnection request in the interconnection queue. Used to prioritize network upgrades when multiple DER projects compete for limited grid capacity.

attributes.name: required_completion_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the network upgrade must be completed to enable the DER interconnection. Drives project scheduling and interconnection agreement milestones.

attributes.name: sgip_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this network upgrade is eligible for cost recovery or incentives under the Self-Generation Incentive Program (SGIP) or similar state DER incentive programs. True if eligible, false otherwise.

attributes.name: shared_cost_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the upgrade cost to be shared between multiple interconnection applicants or beneficiaries, in USD. Used when upgrade benefits multiple DER projects.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system that originated this network upgrade record (e.g., interconnection management system, capital project system, GIS). Identifies the system of record for data lineage.

attributes.name: technical_justification
attributes.description: Engineering rationale explaining why this network upgrade is required to safely accommodate the DER interconnection. Documents the technical need based on impact study results.

attributes.name: upgrade_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the network upgrade scope, including technical specifications, equipment to be installed or modified, and work to be performed.

attributes.name: upgrade_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the network upgrade, typically assigned by engineering or project management systems. Used for external communication and tracking.

attributes.name: upgrade_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the network upgrade project. Tracks progression from initial identification through design, permitting, construction, and completion phases. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: identified|designed|permitted|contracted|in_progress|completed|cancelled — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: upgrade_type
attributes.description: Classification of the type of network upgrade required to accommodate DER interconnection. Defines the nature of the physical grid improvement needed for safe integration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: transformer_upsizing|line_reconductoring|protection_relay_replacement|protection_relay_addition|voltage_regulator_addition|capacitor_bank_addition|communication_infrastructure|transfer_trip|substation_expansion|feeder_extension|other — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: utility_funded_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the upgrade cost to be funded by the utility through rate base or other utility funding mechanisms, in USD. Represents utility's share of network improvement costs.

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Operating voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the grid infrastructure being upgraded. Defines the electrical system tier (distribution vs transmission) affected by the upgrade.

products.name: agreement
products.description: Executed legal agreement between the utility and the DER applicant governing the terms and conditions of grid interconnection. Captures agreement type (Small Generator Interconnection Agreement — SGIA, Large Generator Interconnection Agreement — LGIA, Simplified Interconnection Agreement), execution date, effective date, expiration date, maximum export capacity (kW), metering configuration (net metering, gross metering, bi-directional), NEM program enrollment flag, applicable tariff schedule, indemnification terms, insurance requirements, and termination conditions. This is the SSOT for the contractual interconnection relationship — distinct from the application (pre-approval) and the NEM agreement (billing program enrollment).
products.reference: SGIA / LGIA — FERC Pro Forma Interconnection Agreement

attributes.name: agreement_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the interconnection agreement record. Primary key.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.account. Business justification: Interconnection agreement execution, network upgrade cost billing, insurance certificate expiration notifications, and account-level regulatory compliance reporting all require linking the agreement t

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.feeder. Business justification: Interconnection agreements are binding contracts specifying the POI on a specific feeder. Utilities query all active agreements per feeder for outage coordination, capacity planning, and export limit

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: Interconnection agreements incorporate specific regulatory obligations as binding contractual terms (protection requirements, operating restrictions, reporting duties, IEEE 1547 mandatory functions).

attributes.name: operating_limit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to grid.operating_limit. Business justification: Interconnection agreements specify maximum_export_capacity_kw and maximum_import_capacity_kw that are formally derived from and constrained by the operating limit at the POI. FERC tariff compliance re

attributes.name: pnode_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.pnode. Business justification: The interconnection agreement specifies the pnode for LMP settlement as a binding commercial term. This link enables market settlement reconciliation, FTR allocation, and congestion revenue rights ass

attributes.name: poi_transmission_line_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.line. Business justification: For line-connected generators, the interconnection agreement specifies the exact transmission line as the contractual POI. This link supports outage coordination, line rating impact tracking, and dete

attributes.name: poi_transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.transmission_substation. Business justification: The executed interconnection agreement legally specifies the POI at a transmission substation. This link is required for ongoing operational coordination, outage scheduling, protection setting verific

attributes.name: ppa_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to renewable.ppa_contract. Business justification: Interconnection agreements for PPA projects must reference the PPA contract to coordinate export limits, delivery points, and metering configuration with commercial terms. Critical for FERC compliance

attributes.name: premise_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.premise. Business justification: Interconnection agreements specify the physical point of interconnection at a premise for metering configuration, service territory validation, and operational dispatch authorization. No existing prem

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer or third-party applicant who is the counterparty to this interconnection agreement.

attributes.name: agreement_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the interconnection agreement, used in correspondence and regulatory filings.

attributes.name: agreement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the interconnection agreement. Draft = under negotiation, Pending Execution = awaiting signatures, Executed = signed but not yet effective, Active = in force, Suspended = temporarily inactive, Terminated = ended by mutual consent or breach, Expired = reached end date. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Draft|Pending Execution|Executed|Active|Suspended|Terminated|Expired — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: agreement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the interconnection agreement based on capacity, complexity, and regulatory framework. SGIA = Small Generator Interconnection Agreement (typically <20 MW), LGIA = Large Generator Interconnection Agreement (typically >=20 MW), Simplified for expedited low-impact projects, NEM for net metering programs, Rule 21 for California-specific interconnection, Wholesale for RTO/ISO market participation.
attributes.value_regex: SGIA|LGIA|Simplified Interconnection Agreement|Net Energy Metering Agreement|Rule 21 Agreement|Wholesale Market Interconnection Agreement
attributes.references: FERC Order 2003, FERC Order 2006, California Rule 21, PURPA

attributes.name: applicable_tariff_schedule
attributes.description: Utility rate schedule or tariff code that governs billing and compensation for the interconnected DER. This determines the rates for energy import, export credits, and any standby or interconnection charges.
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff Filings, FERC Rate Schedules

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date on which the DER was commissioned and began commercial operation under this interconnection agreement. This is the actual in-service date, which may differ from the effective date of the agreement.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interconnection agreement record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: customer_funded_upgrade_cost_usd
attributes.description: Portion of network upgrade costs in US dollars that the DER applicant is responsible for funding under the terms of the interconnection agreement. Null if all upgrades are utility-funded.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2003, State PUC Cost Allocation Rules

attributes.name: der_technology_type
attributes.description: Primary technology type of the distributed energy resource covered by this interconnection agreement. Used for portfolio analysis, renewable energy tracking, and compliance reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Solar PV|Wind|Battery Storage|Combined Heat and Power|Fuel Cell|Diesel Generator|Natural Gas Generator|Hydroelectric|Geothermal|EV Charger|Other — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222, IEEE 1547, State Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS)

attributes.name: document_url
attributes.description: URL or file path to the executed interconnection agreement document stored in the enterprise document management system. Used for audit, compliance, and customer service reference.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the interconnection agreement terms become binding and the DER is authorized to interconnect to the grid, subject to all technical and safety requirements being met.

attributes.name: execution_date
attributes.description: Date on which the interconnection agreement was signed by all parties. This is the legal signature date, distinct from the effective date when terms become binding.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the interconnection agreement terminates by its own terms. Nullable for agreements with indefinite term or subject to renewal provisions.

attributes.name: export_limitation_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DER is required to limit or prevent export of power to the grid due to local system constraints, safety concerns, or tariff restrictions. Export limitation may be enforced through inverter settings or physical controls.

attributes.name: indemnification_terms
attributes.description: Summary of the contractual indemnification provisions, specifying which party bears liability for damages, injuries, or losses arising from the operation of the DER or interconnection facilities.
attributes.references: Internal Legal Standard, FERC Standard Interconnection Agreements

attributes.name: insurance_certificate_expiration_date
attributes.description: Expiration date of the current insurance certificate on file for this interconnection agreement. Used to track compliance with ongoing insurance requirements.

attributes.name: insurance_minimum_coverage_usd
attributes.description: Minimum liability insurance coverage amount in US dollars that the DER owner must maintain under the terms of the interconnection agreement. Null if no insurance is required.
attributes.references: FERC Standard Interconnection Agreements, State PUC Requirements

attributes.name: insurance_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the interconnection agreement requires the DER owner to maintain liability insurance coverage as a condition of interconnection.
attributes.references: FERC Standard Interconnection Agreements, State PUC Requirements

attributes.name: interconnection_study_cost_usd
attributes.description: Total cost in US dollars charged to the applicant for interconnection studies (feasibility, system impact, facilities studies). Null if no study was required or cost was waived.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2003, State PUC Interconnection Procedures

attributes.name: interconnection_study_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal interconnection impact study (feasibility, system impact, or facilities study) was required as part of the agreement approval process. Typically required for larger or more complex DER projects.

attributes.name: inverter_certification_standard
attributes.description: Technical standard to which the DER inverter or interconnection equipment is certified, ensuring compliance with grid safety and power quality requirements. Common standards include IEEE 1547-2018, UL 1741, IEC 62109.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interconnection agreement record was last updated in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: maximum_export_capacity_kw
attributes.description: Maximum electrical power in kilowatts that the DER is authorized to export to the utility grid under this interconnection agreement. This is the contractual limit, which may differ from the nameplate capacity of the generation equipment.

attributes.name: maximum_import_capacity_kw
attributes.description: Maximum electrical power in kilowatts that the customer site is authorized to import from the utility grid under this interconnection agreement. Relevant for sites with bi-directional flow such as battery storage or EV charging facilities.

attributes.name: metering_configuration
attributes.description: Type of metering arrangement specified in the interconnection agreement. Net Metering = single meter measuring net flow, Gross Metering = separate meters for import and export, Bi-Directional = single meter capable of measuring both directions, Import Only = consumption only, Export Only = generation only.
attributes.references: PURPA, State Net Energy Metering (NEM) Regulations

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: User ID or name of the person who last modified this interconnection agreement record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: nameplate_capacity_kw
attributes.description: Manufacturer-rated maximum continuous output capacity of the DER equipment in kilowatts. This is the equipment rating, which may differ from the contractual maximum export capacity.

attributes.name: nem_program_enrolled_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Net Energy Metering (NEM) Program Enrolled Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the interconnection agreement includes enrollment in a Net Energy Metering program, allowing the customer to receive bill credits for excess generation exported to the grid.

attributes.name: nem_program_version
attributes.description: Specific version or tariff schedule of the NEM program under which the customer is enrolled (e.g., NEM 2.0, NEM 3.0, grandfathered NEM 1.0). Different versions have different compensation rates and rules.
attributes.references: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) NEM Tariffs

attributes.name: network_upgrade_cost_usd
attributes.description: Estimated or actual cost in US dollars of utility system upgrades required for this interconnection. Cost allocation (customer-funded vs. utility-funded) depends on regulatory framework and agreement type.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2003, State PUC Cost Allocation Rules

attributes.name: network_upgrade_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether utility distribution or transmission system upgrades are required to accommodate the interconnection of this DER. Upgrades may include transformer replacements, line reconductoring, or protection system enhancements.

attributes.name: parallel_operation_allowed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DER is authorized to operate in parallel with the utility grid (exporting power) or is restricted to islanded/backup operation only. Most modern interconnection agreements allow parallel operation.

attributes.name: poi_location_description
attributes.description: Textual description of the physical location where the DER interconnects to the utility distribution or transmission system. Includes substation name, feeder ID, transformer location, or other technical reference points.

attributes.name: poi_voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage in kilovolts at the point where the DER interconnects to the utility system. Common values include 0.12, 0.24, 0.48, 4.16, 12.47, 13.8, 34.5, 69, 115, 138, 230, 345, 500 kV.

attributes.name: sgip_application_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the SGIP or other incentive program application associated with this interconnection agreement. Null if no incentive application exists.

attributes.name: sgip_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DER project is eligible for California Self-Generation Incentive Program rebates or other state/federal incentive programs. Used for customer incentive tracking and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: California SGIP Guidelines, State Energy Incentive Programs

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the interconnection agreement was terminated prior to its natural expiration, due to breach, mutual consent, or other contractual provisions. Null if agreement has not been terminated.

attributes.name: termination_reason
attributes.description: Business reason or contractual clause under which the interconnection agreement was terminated. Examples include breach of terms, failure to maintain insurance, decommissioning of DER, customer request, or utility system changes.

attributes.name: witness_test_date
attributes.description: Date on which the utility conducted a witness test or commissioning inspection to verify that the DER installation meets all technical and safety requirements specified in the interconnection agreement.

attributes.name: witness_test_result
attributes.description: Outcome of the utility witness test or commissioning inspection. Passed = DER meets all requirements, Failed = deficiencies identified, Conditional Pass = minor issues to be resolved, Not Required = test waived for low-impact projects, Pending = test scheduled but not yet completed.

products.name: nem_agreement
products.description: Net Energy Metering (NEM) program enrollment agreement for a customer with an approved DER interconnection. Captures NEM program type (NEM 1.0, NEM 2.0, NEM 3.0 / NEM-ST, VNEM for virtual NEM, NEMA for NEM aggregation), enrollment date, true-up period (monthly, annual), export compensation rate (retail rate, avoided cost, NEM tariff rate), banking credits policy, maximum system size eligibility, applicable PUC tariff schedule, and program expiration date. Distinct from the interconnection agreement (technical/legal) — the NEM agreement governs the billing and compensation mechanism for exported energy.
products.reference: NEM (Net Energy Metering) Enrollment Agreement — PUC Tariff

attributes.name: nem_agreement_id
attributes.description: Primary key for nem_agreement

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.account. Business justification: NEM billing credits, export compensation, and annual true-up calculations are account-level financial transactions requiring direct account linkage for billing system integration and credit reconcilia

attributes.name: agreement_id
attributes.description: Reference to the technical interconnection agreement that governs the physical connection of the DER to the utility grid. The NEM agreement governs billing and compensation; the interconnection agreement governs technical and safety requirements.

attributes.name: customer_service_agreement_id
attributes.description: Reference to the billing service agreement under which NEM credits and charges are applied.

attributes.name: der_system_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to interconnection.der_system. Business justification: A NEM agreement is established for a specific DER system. The nem_agreement has installed_system_size_kw and der_technology_type that describe the DER system enrolled in NEM. Linking nem_agreement to

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.feeder. Business justification: NEM program administration requires feeder-level tracking of enrolled customers for export credit calculations, feeder NEM capacity caps, and annual true-up reporting. Utilities must know which feeder

attributes.name: meter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the bi-directional meter installed at the customer premises to measure both energy consumption and generation for NEM billing purposes.

attributes.name: nem_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to renewable.nem_account. Business justification: Billing and settlement systems must link the formal NEM interconnection agreement to the operational NEM account for export credit calculations, banking policy application, and annual true-up reconcil

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: NEM agreements implement specific regulatory obligations from state NEM programs (tariff compliance, metering requirements, reporting rules, RPS credit eligibility). Essential for tracking program com

attributes.name: premise_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.premise. Business justification: NEM agreement governs export compensation at a specific service premise. Premise FK enables NEM export limit enforcement at the feeder level, premise-level NEM aggregation for hosting capacity, and IC

attributes.name: primary_nem_interconnection_application_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent interconnection application that this NEM agreement is associated with.

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer who owns the Distributed Energy Resource (DER) and is enrolled in the NEM program.

attributes.name: rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.rate_schedule. Business justification: NEM agreements are governed by specific rate schedules that determine export compensation rates and billing terms. nem_agreement has denormalized tariff_schedule_code and tariff_schedule_name columns;

attributes.name: annual_true_up_month
attributes.description: The calendar month (1-12) in which the annual NEM true-up reconciliation occurs for customers on annual true-up billing. Null for monthly true-up customers.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the utility approved the customer's NEM agreement application.

attributes.name: banking_credits_policy
attributes.description: The policy governing how excess NEM credits are carried forward. Indefinite (credits roll over indefinitely until used), Annual Expiration (credits expire at annual true-up), Monthly Expiration (credits expire at end of each billing cycle), No Banking (no credit carryover, excess generation compensated at lower rate).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this NEM agreement record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: cumulative_credit_balance_kwh
attributes.description: The current cumulative balance of NEM energy credits in kilowatt-hours (kWh) that the customer has banked and not yet consumed. Updated after each billing cycle.

attributes.name: cumulative_credit_balance_usd
attributes.description: The current cumulative monetary value in US dollars of NEM credits that the customer has banked and not yet applied to billing charges. Updated after each billing cycle.

attributes.name: der_technology_type
attributes.description: The primary technology type of the DER system covered by this NEM agreement. Solar PV (photovoltaic solar panels), Wind (small wind turbine), Battery Storage (standalone or paired with generation), Fuel Cell (hydrogen or natural gas fuel cell), Combined Heat and Power (CHP cogeneration), Micro Hydro (small-scale hydroelectric).

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Net Energy Metering (NEM) Effective End Date
attributes.description: The date on which the NEM agreement expires or is terminated. Null for open-ended agreements or active agreements without a defined end date.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Net Energy Metering (NEM) Effective Start Date
attributes.description: The date from which NEM billing and credit calculations begin. May differ from enrollment date if retroactive application is approved.

attributes.name: enrollment_date
attributes.description: The date the customer was officially enrolled in the NEM program and the agreement became effective.

attributes.name: export_compensation_rate
attributes.description: The per-kilowatt-hour (kWh) rate at which the customer is compensated for energy exported to the grid, expressed in dollars per kWh.

attributes.name: export_compensation_rate_type
attributes.description: The methodology used to compensate the customer for energy exported to the grid. Retail Rate (full retail electricity rate, typical for NEM 1.0), Avoided Cost (utility's avoided cost of generation, typical for NEM 3.0), NEM Tariff Rate (specific tariff rate defined by PUC for NEM program), Wholesale Rate (market-based wholesale energy price).

attributes.name: grandfathered_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this NEM agreement is grandfathered under a previous program version's terms and conditions, protecting the customer from changes in subsequent tariff revisions. True if grandfathered, False otherwise.

attributes.name: grandfathered_until_date
attributes.description: The date until which the grandfathered status is valid. After this date, the customer may be transitioned to the current NEM program terms. Null if not grandfathered or if grandfathering is indefinite.

attributes.name: installed_system_size_kw
attributes.description: The actual nameplate capacity in kilowatts (kW) of the customer's installed DER system as verified during interconnection inspection.

attributes.name: interconnection_agreement
attributes.description: FK to interconnection.agreement.agreement_id — NEM enrollment requires an executed interconnection agreement. The NEM agreement references the underlying interconnection agreement for the same DER system.

attributes.name: last_true_up_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent NEM true-up reconciliation for this agreement.

attributes.name: maximum_system_size_kw
attributes.description: The maximum nameplate capacity in kilowatts (kW) of the customer's Distributed Energy Resource (DER) system that is eligible for NEM under this agreement. Typically based on customer's historical peak demand or regulatory cap.

attributes.name: nem_program_type
attributes.description: The specific NEM program version under which the customer is enrolled. NEM 1.0 (legacy retail rate compensation), NEM 2.0 (retail rate minus non-bypassable charges), NEM 3.0 / NEM-ST (successor tariff with export compensation based on avoided cost), VNEM (Virtual Net Energy Metering for multi-tenant or community solar), NEMA (NEM Aggregation for multiple meters under single customer).
attributes.references: CPUC Decision 14-03-041, CPUC Decision 16-01-044, CPUC Decision 21-12-006

attributes.name: nema_aggregation_type
attributes.description: For NEM Aggregation (NEMA) agreements, the type of meter aggregation allowed. On Site (multiple meters on same parcel), Adjacent Parcels (meters on contiguous parcels owned by same customer), Same Customer (meters under same customer account within service territory). Null for non-NEMA agreements.

attributes.name: next_true_up_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date of the next NEM true-up reconciliation for this agreement.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, comments, or special conditions related to the NEM agreement.

attributes.name: poi_location
attributes.description: The physical location description of the Point of Interconnection where the customer's DER system connects to the utility distribution grid.

attributes.name: program_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the NEM agreement. Pending (application submitted, awaiting approval), Active (agreement in force, customer receiving NEM credits), Suspended (temporarily inactive due to non-compliance or system outage), Terminated (customer or utility ended agreement), Expired (agreement reached end of term).

attributes.name: sgip_incentive_eligible_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Self-Generation Incentive Program (SGIP) Incentive Eligible Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DER system under this NEM agreement is eligible for Self-Generation Incentive Program (SGIP) incentives. True if eligible, False otherwise.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: The date on which the NEM agreement was terminated by the customer or utility. Null if agreement is still active.

attributes.name: termination_reason
attributes.description: The reason for termination of the NEM agreement (e.g., customer request, system decommissioned, non-compliance, property sale). Null if agreement is still active.

attributes.name: to_agreement
attributes.description: FK to interconnection.agreement.agreement_id — NEM enrollment is contingent on having an executed interconnection agreement. The NEM agreement governs billing/compensation while the interconnection agreement governs technical/legal terms. They are

attributes.name: true_up_period
attributes.description: The billing cycle frequency at which net energy consumption and generation are reconciled and excess credits are settled. Monthly (credits reconciled each billing cycle), Annual (credits accumulated over 12 months and reconciled at year-end).

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this NEM agreement record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: vnem_allocation_method
attributes.business_glossary_term: Virtual Net Energy Metering (VNEM) Allocation Method
attributes.description: For Virtual NEM (VNEM) agreements, the method by which generation credits are allocated among multiple beneficiary accounts. Proportional (based on each account's usage), Fixed Percentage (predefined allocation percentages), Custom (customer-defined allocation rules). Null for non-VNEM agreements.

products.name: application_status_history
products.description: Audit trail record capturing each lifecycle state transition and formal regulatory communication for an interconnection application from submission through final disposition. Captures prior status, new status, transition timestamp, triggering event (applicant action, utility action, regulatory deadline, formal communication sent/received), responsible party, communication type (deficiency notice, completeness determination, study offer letter, cost estimate letter, agreement offer, PTO notification, withdrawal notice), communication channel, response deadline, response received flag, comments, and days elapsed in each status. Enables queue management SLA tracking, FERC Order 2023 milestone compliance reporting (completeness determination within 10 business days, study offer within 30 days, etc.), regulatory communication audit trail, and identification of bottlenecks in the interconnection review process.
products.reference: Interconnection Queue Status Tracking

attributes.name: application_status_history_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each status transition record in the interconnection application lifecycle audit trail.

attributes.name: primary_interconnection_application_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent interconnection application for which this status transition occurred.

attributes.name: tertiary_application_id
attributes.description: FK to interconnection.application.application_id — Status history records are audit trail entries FOR a specific application. This is the most obvious parent-child FK in the domain.

attributes.name: business_days_in_prior_status
attributes.description: Number of business days (excluding weekends and holidays) the application remained in the prior status, used for regulatory compliance milestone tracking per FERC Order 2023.

attributes.name: communication_channel
attributes.description: The medium or channel through which the formal communication was sent or received during this status transition.

attributes.name: communication_received_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when a response or acknowledgment communication was received from the applicant or other party, recorded in ISO 8601 format.

attributes.name: communication_reference_number
attributes.description: Unique tracking number or identifier assigned to the formal communication document associated with this status transition, enabling audit trail linkage.

attributes.name: communication_sent_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the formal communication was sent to the applicant or other party, recorded in ISO 8601 format.

attributes.name: communication_type
attributes.description: Type of formal regulatory or business communication associated with this status transition. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: deficiency_notice|completeness_determination|study_offer_letter|cost_estimate_letter|agreement_offer|pto_notification|withdrawal_notice|information_request|technical_review_report|impact_study_report|feasibility_study_report|system_impact_study|facilities_study — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this status transition record was first created in the system, recorded in ISO 8601 format for audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: days_in_prior_status
attributes.description: Number of calendar days the application remained in the prior status before this transition occurred, used for SLA tracking and bottleneck analysis.

attributes.name: internal_notes
attributes.description: Confidential internal notes recorded by utility staff regarding this status transition, not shared with the applicant, used for internal coordination and decision documentation.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this status transition record was last modified in the system, recorded in ISO 8601 format for audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: new_status
attributes.description: The status of the interconnection application after this transition, representing the current state following the triggering event. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: submitted|under_review|incomplete|study_in_progress|study_complete|agreement_pending|approved — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: notification_sent_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether an automated notification was sent to the applicant or other stakeholders regarding this status transition.

attributes.name: notification_sent_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the automated notification was sent to stakeholders regarding this status transition, recorded in ISO 8601 format.

attributes.name: prior_status
attributes.description: The status of the interconnection application immediately before this transition occurred. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: submitted|under_review|incomplete|study_in_progress|study_complete|agreement_pending|approved — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: queue_position
attributes.description: The position of the interconnection application in the utility interconnection queue at the time of this status transition, used for queue management and priority tracking.

attributes.name: regulatory_milestone_met_flag

Captures queue number (utility-assigned sequential identifier), queue entry date, queue position, study group assignment (for cluster/group study processes), queue withdrawal date (if applicable), withdrawal reason, queue hold status, and estimated study completion date. Manages the orderly processing of DER interconnection requests per FERC Order 2023 cluster study rules and state PUC interconnection procedures. One queue record per application.

products.name: hosting_capacity
products.description: Hosting capacity assessment record for a distribution circuit, feeder segment, or substation load area, capturing the maximum additional DER capacity (kW) that can be interconnected at that location without triggering network upgrades. Captures feeder/circuit identifier, node or segment location, assessment date, thermal hosting capacity (kW), voltage hosting capacity (kW), protection hosting capacity (kW), binding constraint type (thermal, voltage, protection coordination, power quality), assessment methodology (deterministic, stochastic, time-series), daytime minimum load assumption, confidence level, data vintage, next scheduled reassessment date, and publication status for public hosting capacity maps per CPUC Rule 21 / ICA or equivalent state requirements. Updated after major network reconfigurations, DER additions, or load changes. Enables applicant self-screening and utility pre-screening of POI feasibility before formal application submission.
products.reference: Distribution Hosting Capacity Analysis (CPUC Rule 21 / IEEE 1547)

attributes.name: assessment_date
attributes.description: Date when the hosting capacity assessment was performed or published.

attributes.name: assessment_methodology
attributes.description: The analytical methodology used to calculate hosting capacity: deterministic (worst-case snapshot), stochastic (probabilistic scenarios), time-series (chronological simulation), or hybrid approach.

attributes.name: assessment_software_tool
attributes.description: Name and version of the software tool or platform used to perform the hosting capacity analysis (e.g., EPRI DRIVE, OpenDSS, CYME, Synergi Electric).

attributes.name: available_hosting_capacity_kw
attributes.description: Net available hosting capacity in kilowatts (kW) after accounting for existing and queued DER capacity. This is the capacity available for new interconnection applications without triggering network upgrades.

attributes.name: binding_constraint_type
attributes.description: The type of network constraint that limits the hosting capacity at this location. Identifies which technical factor (thermal, voltage, protection coordination, power quality, stability) is the bottleneck.

attributes.name: confidence_level_percent
attributes.description: Statistical confidence level (as a percentage) associated with the hosting capacity estimate, particularly relevant for stochastic or probabilistic assessments. For example, 95% confidence means the capacity is available 95% of the time under modeled conditions.

attributes.name: data_vintage_date

attributes.name: daytime_minimum_load_kw
attributes.description: The assumed daytime minimum load in kilowatts (kW) used in the hosting capacity calculation. Critical for assessing reverse power flow and overvoltage risk from solar generation during low-load periods.

attributes.name: der_type_scope
attributes.description: The type(s) of Distributed Energy Resource (DER) for which this hosting capacity assessment applies. May be specific to solar PV, battery storage, EV chargers, or applicable to all DER types.

attributes.name: existing_der_capacity_kw
